detail.title: From Paper to Pixels: The Legal and Practical Transition of Bills of Exchange in India, the UK, and International Trade.

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no financial, commercial, or personal conflicts of interest that could have influenced or biased the research, analysis, or conclusions presented in this paper.

detail.abstract: Bills of exchange have historically served as a foundational instrument for credit facilitation and commercial transactions, both domestically and across borders. This paper examines the statutory framework governing bills of exchange in India under the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, and evaluates the ongoing transition from paper-based to electronic transferable records. By comparing India's regulatory trajectory with jurisdictions that have enacted statutory frameworks for digital trade documents, notably the United Kingdom, the study situates both approaches within the international architecture of UNCITRAL's Model Law on Electronic Transferable Records (MLETR), while also examining the instrument's continuing domestic function as a credit tool. Finally, it analyses key doctrinal, operational, and cross-border frictions inherent to this shift and outlines strategic recommendations for the broader international adoption of electronic trade document frameworks.

title: Responsible Food Production and Sustainable Consumption in Italian Restaurants: A Pathway to SDG 12
affiliations: University of Malta, University of Rome "La Sapienza", University of Rome "La Sapienza", University of Rome "La Sapienza", University of L'Aquila and University of Rome "La Sapienza"

detail.title: Responsible Food Production and Sustainable Consumption in Italian Restaurants: A Pathway to SDG 12

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.funderStatement: No funding was required.

detail.abstract: The pursuit of sustainable business approaches has gained increasing importance in the past years. Entrepreneurs are increasingly reassessing their strategies and operations in line with corporate social and environmental responsibility principles. Restaurants are well positioned to play a key role as agents for positive change, as they can offer nutritious, high-quality food. At the same time, they could minimize food loss and waste. They may even contribute to local economic development through the promotion of short supply chains among other responsible practices. This study examines consumer behaviours and perceptions of responsible food production and sustainable consumption within the Italian hospitality industry. It focuses on factors that influence the consumers' dining choices and their willingness to engage in environmentally responsible actions. The research adopts a social analysis perspective based on data collected from an online survey of 609 respondents in Italy. The findings indicate that consumer decisions are primarily motivated by hedonic factors, especially taste and the quality of ingredients. Awareness of sustainable practices tends to increase by time and is more evidenced among women, who also show a greater propensity to adjust their habits in more sustainable ways. Despite a general interest in sustainability and a willingness to pay a premium for certified establishments, there remains a limited understanding of restaurants' environmental impacts and low familiarity with sustainability certifications. These research implications highlight considerable opportunities for growth. This contribution postulates that enhanced communication strategies and targeted awareness campaigns could improve consumer knowledge, foster more informed choices and encourage active support for sustainability initiatives in the restaurant sector, in line with Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 12.

title: Question Zero: Why Responsible AI Begins Before AI Adoption

detail.abstract: The Question Zero (Q0) Self-Assessment Tool for Responsible AI, developed by the AI Policy Lab at Umeå University, supports organisations in posing foundational questions before adopting AI. Grounded in the concept of Question Zero: "Under what conditions should an AI system be adopted, if at all?", the tool offers support for cross-functional team discussions covering motivation, stakeholder mapping, system type, adoption process and infrastructure. It is designed for public institutions, civil society organisations, policymakers and other actors looking for responsible AI decision-making approaches. With the help of the tool, we argue that purposeful, problem-led assessment must precede any procurement and deployment decisions.

title: Boundary Design in Agentic Organizations
affiliations: University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign - Gies College of Business,  and University of Florida - Warrington College of Business Administration

detail.title: Boundary Design in Agentic Organizations

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: As employees increasingly work with AI agents, these agents gradually learn their users' routines, judgment, and domain expertise. Over time, an employee's agent can carry part of that productive capability and become, in an economically meaningful sense, a partial working clone of its user. This raises a new organizational design question: how freely should an employee's working clone be allowed to serve that employee's colleagues? More open agent boundaries allow valuable capability to travel across the organization, but can also weaken employees' incentives to build it. We develop an analytical model of agent boundary openness to study this tension between capability creation and redeployment. We find that greater openness need not discourage capability creation: when employees' capabilities have sufficiently valuable uses across coworkers' workflows, opening agent boundaries can strengthen their incentives to build. More importantly, the organization may optimally open agent boundaries beyond the point at which further openness begins to depress capability creation, because each remaining unit of capability can be deployed more effectively. The boundary that maximizes capability creation therefore need not maximize organizational value. Consequently, connecting previously isolated personal agents can lead employees to build less capability while still increasing organizational value. More broadly, our findings point to a new layer of organizational governance introduced by agentic AI. Organizations must govern not only what AI agents can do, but also how freely the capabilities they carry can move across the organization. Agent boundary design provides a governance lever for managing this capability flow and its incentive consequences.

detail.abstract: A supply chain does not move by itself. Every movement of material, information, or money happens because someone made a decision, under conditions that made the decision sensible at the time. When those conditions change, the decision may no longer be valid even though the process executing it carries on working normally. This article proposes Supply Chain Decision Flow (SCDF) as an architectural approach for keeping consequential decisions valid, connected, and coordinated as conditions change.

title:

Why Symbolic Management Support Fails to Translate into Performance Gains

Why Symbolic Management Support Fails to Translate into Performance Gains

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest
declarations.funderStatement: Not funded

detail.abstract: Top management support (TMS) is widely cited as essential for procurement reform, yet public universities in Nairobi report persistent inefficiencies. The objective of this study was to test whether TMS yields performance gains only when backed by substantive resource provision and clear policy support. Descriptive mixed-methods research design. It used a stratified random sample of 213 staff across procurement, finance and administration in five Nairobi public universities; questionnaires (5-1 Likert), pilot (n=22) and semi-structured interviews with 15 procurement directors drawn from the universities. Quantitative analysis was done via multiple linear regression in Python 3.14.4. Quantitative results showed that top management support was statistically insignificant (β= 0.1520, t = 1.2060, p = 0.2298, CI = [-0.0971, 0.4012]). Resource allocation (RA) had a positive and significant effect (β = 0.3702, t = 4.3923, p = 0.0000, CI = [0.2037, 0.5368]). It was concluded that leadership commitment is necessary but insufficient; substantive resource provision operationalizes commitment and drives procurement performance.

title: Diaspora Political Marketing on Encrypted Platforms Beyond Borders: Diaspora Communities as a New Frontier of Political Marketing on Encrypted Messaging Platforms A Qualitative Comparative Case Study of WhatsApp and Telegram in Contemporary Election Campaigns

detail.title: Diaspora Political Marketing on Encrypted Platforms Beyond Borders: Diaspora Communities as a New Frontier of Political Marketing on Encrypted Messaging Platforms A Qualitative Comparative Case Study of WhatsApp and Telegram in Contemporary Election Campaigns

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interest.
declarations.funderStatement: the author is self funded

detail.abstract: Political marketing has extensively documented the shift toward digital, data-driven, and relationshipbased campaigning, yet the role of encrypted messaging platforms principally WhatsApp and Telegram in mobilizing diaspora and expatriate voters remains comparatively under-examined. This paper adopts a qualitative, multiple-case-study approach to examine how recent political campaigns in New York City (2025), Romania (2024), and India, alongside contrasting disinformation and regulatory episodes in the United States and Spain, have marketed to diaspora communities through closed, encrypted, peer-to-peer channels. Drawing on journalistic investigations, platform behavior research, and publicly available electoral data, the paper identifies four cross-cutting themes: the leveraging of family and community trust networks as an informal media channel; the use of language and cultural code-switching as an implicit segmentation tool; the double-edged nature of encryption, which enables both grassroots mobilization and unaccountable disinformation; and the growing electoral weight of diaspora populations, illustrated starkly by Romania's 2024 presidential election, where diaspora support for one candidate nearly doubled the domestic figure. The paper concludes with implications for political marketing theory and practice and proposes an agenda for future primary research.

title: Same Yen Move, Different Shock: A Mechanism-Separated Design for FX Intervention, Monetary Repricing, and Carry Unwinds

detail.title: Same Yen Move, Different Shock: A Mechanism-Separated Design for FX Intervention, Monetary Repricing, and Carry Unwinds

detail.abstract: This design paper starts from a simple empirical difficulty: the same yen appreciation can be produced by very different shocks. Market commentary often compresses official intervention, a carry-trade unwind, JGB repricing, and a broad dollar move into one narrative. That compression is precisely what the paper asks the data to resist. It separates confirmed yen-buying intervention, intervention anticipation without an executed transaction, Bank of Japan monetary-policy repricing, and global dollar or risk shocks. The design combines official intervention records with high-frequency USD/JPY prices, JGB yields across the curve, interest-rate expectations, option-implied risk measures, and returns on representative carry targets. Its empirical question is whether these mechanisms leave different intraday signatures, cross-asset responses, and persistence profiles. Intervention entry, immediate impact, and persistence are separate estimands; a carry claim must also identify the funding leg, target asset, holding horizon, and realized return condition. The 2026 episode-including the record ¥15.3993 trillion monthly intervention total and a subsequent sharp yen appreciation without confirmed intervention-provides the motivation. The historical date-amount audit is complete, but causal inference remains conditional on execution-time measurement and the limits of the available comparison design. The first implementation supplies a 5-minute market-data diagnostic for seven 2022-2024 operation dates and a daily cash-carry panel with explicit funding and target legs. The intraday diagnostic identifies market-implied breaks, not official transaction timestamps.

title: A Preliminary Study on Image Fusion for Snow-pole Detection in Machine-sensible Winter Infrastructure
affiliations: , Eindhoven University of Technology, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Shanghai University of Electric Power

detail.title: A Preliminary Study on Image Fusion for Snow-pole Detection in Machine-sensible Winter Infrastructure

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors also sincerely thank Frank Lindseth and Gabriel Hanssen Kiss of NTNU for their support during Durga Prasad Bavirisetti’s postdoctoral research period, particularly in vehi- cle setup, data collection, and technical discussions. Although they were not involved in the present study, their earlier contributions are gratefully acknowledged.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was supported by the Knowledge Foundation (KKS), Sweden, under the project “Digital Image Analysis and Artificial Intelligence” (Contract No. KKS-20230085). The authors would like to acknowledge the Norwegian Re- search Council project “Machine Sensible Infrastructure under Nordic Conditions” (Project No. 333875), which contributed to the development of publicly available resources used in this work.

detail.abstract: Reliable snow-pole detection is critical for infrastructure-assisted perception and vehicle localization in Nordic winter environments, where snow cover, low illumination, and radiometric variability significantly degrade visual contrast and structural visibility. This paper presents a controlled preliminary study investigating the effect of classical multimodal image fusion on downstream snow-pole detection using three co-registered LiDAR-derived modalities: signal, reflectivity, and near-infrared. A diverse set of conventional fusion strategies-including pixel-level operators, PCA-based fusion, multi-scale pyramids, adaptive filtering, and CLAHE-enhanced variants-is evaluated within a unified YOLOv11n detection framework. The study is intentionally designed as a systematic baseline analysis, isolating the influence of fusion mechanisms prior to introducing complex learning-based fusion architectures. Experimental results show that fusion does not inherently guarantee improved detection performance. Quantitative gains over the standalone Signal modality are modest; however, this observation provides a key engineering insight: task-aligned modality weighting is substantially more important than generic fusion operators. Fusion strategies that emphasize the Signal channel while preserving pole-relevant structural features consistently outperform naive statistical or multi-scale combinations, whereas indiscriminate fusion may introduce artifacts that degrade localization robustness. These findings establish an essential reference point for winter infrastructure perception and highlight the need for task-aware fusion design. All fused datasets, pretrained weights, and code will be publicly released to support reproducible research and future development of learning-based multimodal fusion for machine-sensible infrastructure under adverse winter conditions.

title:
Full-coverage Low-Earth-orbit Desert Shading: 
Exploring the Hypothesis of Desert Transition and Ecological Succession Toward Shrubland, Oasis, and Primeval Forest Under Full Shading

detail.title:
Full-coverage Low-Earth-orbit Desert Shading: 
Exploring the Hypothesis of Desert Transition and Ecological Succession Toward Shrubland, Oasis, and Primeval Forest Under Full Shading

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest. This is independent research with no financial or personal relationships that could be perceived to have influenced this work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This is a theoretical/conceptual paper involving no human participants, patient data, or case studies requiring ethics approval.

detail.abstract: The companion paper (LX-DSRM-FULL v0.2) established that full areal reflective coverage of Earth’s desert biome (hyper-arid + arid land, ≈29.2 million km²) is not excluded by orbital mechanics or historical technology-growth trends, on a multi-century civilizational timescale (≈125–330 years under plausible capacity-growth curves), while leaving open whether such coverage would be climatically or ecologically beneficial. This revision, at the author’s explicit direction, asks a more specific and more ambitious question: could full-coverage shading not merely reduce potential evapotranspiration (PET) at desert margins, but actively drive ecological succession — bare desert → pioneer shrub → established shrubland/oasis →, in the longest and most speculative case, closed-canopy woodland approaching primeval-forest structure — across meaningful portions of the target zone? We keep this as the paper’s central hypothesis and do not retreat from it. We also state, as an unavoidable physical consequence of taking the hypothesis seriously rather than asserting it uncritically, that literal permanent 100% optical opacity is self-defeating for this specific goal: photosynthesis requires photosynthetically active radiation (PAR), so a shading system whose purpose is to enable plant succession cannot, at the same time, be a permanent full blackout — “full coverage” in this paper therefore denotes near-total areal deployment across the target zone combined with adaptive, partial, and spectrally selective optical modulation (reducing thermal and evaporative stress while preserving a working PAR budget), not total light exclusion. With that correction stated plainly, we find the succession hypothesis physically coherent for the arid category (≈18.0 million km², where a non-zero precipitation floor already exists) and for select semi-arid-adjacent margins, with succession timescales of decades (pioneer shrub establishment) to multiple centuries (closed-canopy, forest-like structure, by analogy with the slowest-known real-world afforestation precedents). We find it physically incoherent, and state this without qualification, for the hyper-arid core (≈11.2 million km², where precipitation itself is near zero): no plausible reduction in evaporative demand substitutes for the absence of water, and this paper does not claim otherwise for that subset of the target zone. The unresolved Charney (1975) versus Li et al. (2018) tension over desert-heating’s effect on monsoon moisture transport, carried over from the companion papers, remains the paper’s other central open question, now compounded by the fact that a successful succession outcome depends on that very moisture transport not being suppressed by the shading intervention itself.

title: United States — A 50-State Analysis of Corporate Tax Structure, Litigation & Liability Costs, Corporate-Law Infrastructure, and Governance Risk for Business Formation and Headquarters Decisions

detail.title: United States — A 50-State Analysis of Corporate Tax Structure, Litigation & Liability Costs, Corporate-Law Infrastructure, and Governance Risk for Business Formation and Headquarters Decisions

The analysis is independently prepared by the author.

declarations.funderStatement: This research was self-funded by the author. No external funding, grant, sponsorship, or commissioned research funding was received for the preparation of this working paper.

detail.abstract:
The United States runs fifty parallel competitions for company formations, headquarters relocations, and reincorporations, each state setting its own corporate code, tax base, court system, and enforcement culture under a single federal floor of income tax and — as of 2025-2026 — a sharply narrowed federal disclosure regime.

This report benchmarks all 50 states across four dimensions and combines them into the U.S. State Formation & Governance Competitiveness Index ("FGCI-US"), introduced in Section 4. Earlier work on this index weighted tax competitiveness and litigation cost most heavily. This edition rebuilds the weighting around a simpler, evidence-led premise: real incorporation behavior — where companies actually file, not where a cost model says they should — is overwhelmingly explained by corporate-law quality and capital-markets confidence, not by tax. Section 4.4 sets out the evidence and the reweighting it justifies.

On corporate law: following Delaware Court of Chancery rulings invalidating Elon Musk's Tesla pay package and related decisions applying heightened scrutiny to controller transactions [1], a record share of public companies with reincorporation proposals on the 2025 proxy ballot proposed leaving Delaware — mostly for Nevada — prompting Delaware's Senate Bill 21 within weeks and a Delaware Supreme Court ruling in early 2026 upholding its constitutionality (Section 6) [2,3]. Even amid that pressure, Delaware's formation volume and Fortune 500 share have not meaningfully eroded [4] — evidence, read alongside Section 4.4, that the threat of departure has moved faster than actual departure.

On tax: the Tax Foundation's 2026 State Tax Competitiveness Index ranks Wyoming, South Dakota, and New Hampshire at the top and New York, New Jersey, and California at the bottom [5] — real, and still weighted into the FGCI-US, but Section 4.4's formation-volume data shows this ranking predicts which states attract small, closely-held, and asset-holding entities far better than it predicts which states attract growth companies raising institutional capital.

On litigation and liability cost: the U.S. Chamber Institute for Legal Reform's Tort Costs in America data [6,7] — which puts Delaware's liability-system cost, as a share of state GDP, highest of any state — is retained at the lowest weight of the four components in this edition, because it measures general tort and mass-tort exposure, not the corporate and shareholder litigation that actually determines where a growth company incorporates (Section 2.2).

On governance risk: using the Cato Institute's compilation of federal public-corruption convictions per 10,000 state and local government employees (2004-2023) as a directional proxy, Louisiana, Montana, and West Virginia carry the highest measured conviction rates and New Hampshire, Utah, and Oregon the lowest [8] — a high conviction rate can as easily indicate vigorous enforcement as high underlying corruption, and Section 8 gives this component the widest caveat of the four.

title: Who Profited from Colonial Entrepreneurship? Evidence from the Congo Free State
affiliations: University of Antwerp

detail.title: Who Profited from Colonial Entrepreneurship? Evidence from the Congo Free State

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding

detail.abstract: This paper examines who profited from colonial entrepreneurship by analyzing the financial performance of all 37 Congo Free State (CFS) ventures listed on the Brussels and Antwerp stock exchanges. Returns from colonial enterprise varied sharply across firms and between participants entering the same ventures at different stages of their development. Company founders generally earned substantial pre-listing gains, particularly in concessionary firms that were partially owned by the CFS. After listing, however, public investors in most CFS ventures earned negative market-adjusted returns. Exceptions were the main colonial holding company operating in the CFS and two of its affiliated firms. CFS stocks initially provided diversification benefits, but these disappeared after 1898.

title: Buying a Station or Relaxing a Constraint? Spectrum Repacking and Dirac’s Conjecture
affiliations: Harvard University

detail.title: Buying a Station or Relaxing a Constraint? Spectrum Repacking and Dirac’s Conjecture

declarations.funderStatement: Funding for this research was provided in part by Harvard Business School.

publicationDetails.detailsText: Harvard Business School Working Paper No. 27-020

detail.abstract: Spectrum repacking auctions can restore feasibility along two margins: retiring a station via buyout or relaxing a pairwise engineering restriction. I represent stations as vertices in a network and interference restrictions as edges between them, and so station buyouts delete vertices and engineering waivers relax edges. This paper shows that buying out any one station can reduce the number of channels needed, even though relaxing any single interference restriction cannot. The smallest feasible number of channels is k. For every k ≥ 4, I show that there is a network in  which removing any station saves one channel, while relaxing any single pairwise restriction does not. This main result follows directly from Dirac’s half-century-old conjecture on vertex-critical graphs, whose chromatic number falls after any vertex is removed. By constructing the missing counterexample at k = 4 and combining it with earlier results for k ≥ 5, I show that at every k ≥ 4, some k-vertex-critical graph has no critical edge, resolving Dirac’s  conjecture. Market designers auditing feasibility link-by-link systematically can mistake combinatorial complementarity for remedy failure, overlooking station buyouts that unlock the clearing target.

title: How digital platforms shape innovation adoption? Role of information design vs. social visibility design
affiliations: Nova School of Business and Economics, University of Auckland Business School and Nova School of Business and Economics

detail.title: How digital platforms shape innovation adoption? Role of information design vs. social visibility design

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

publicationDetails.detailsText: Nova SBE Working Paper Series No. 684

detail.abstract: Digital platforms increasingly mediate how consumers adopt new products, services, and technologies. Platforms shape adoption-relevant preference through two design levers: information design (through product pages, personalized recommendations, tutorials, and sponsored content), which affects users' private evaluation and social visibility design (through reviews, ratings, rankings, badges, and algorithmic feeds) which affects users' social evaluation. We ask when each lever is more effective in platform-mediated innovation adoption. We develop an analytical model that incorporates social factors such as homophily, and identity-based reference-group effects to identify the boundary conditions under which information design or social visibility design has the larger effect. The model shows that social visibility design can dominate information design when social evaluation carries more weight than private evaluation. It also shows that social visibility design is double-edged: it amplifies prevailing average preference, is strengthened by homophily, and can backfire when visible adopters are associated with dissociative reference groups. When social visibility design becomes sufficiently strong, the model predicts critical-mass effects and path dependence, so that platforms with similar information design intensity can produce different long-run adoption outcomes. Simulations complement the analytical propositions by mapping the parameter regions in which each equilibrium result emerges.

title: Asymmetric Over- and Underreaction to Good and Bad News
affiliations: University of Warwick - Warwick Business School and

detail.title: Asymmetric Over- and Underreaction to Good and Bad News

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no financial or personal relationships that could have influenced the research reported in this paper
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Applying the error-revision framework of Coibion and Gorodnichenko (2015) to sell-side analysts' earnings forecast revisions, we show that beliefs overreact to good news but underreact to bad. On the analyst side, the asymmetry is consistent with motivated beliefs and incentives to be optimistic: around broker mergers, an exogenous shock to optimism pressure, analysts' reaction functions tilt further toward optimism. On the firm side, the asymmetry varies predictably with characteristics from the cross-sectional asset-pricing literature, notably momentum and volatility, suggesting that these anomalies are related to sign-dependent belief errors. The asymmetry also matters for prices. It predicts cumulative abnormal returns of about 100 basis points around earnings announcements, consistent with expectational errors being corrected when earnings are revealed. It also helps explain where momentum arises: winners continue when analysts overreact less to good news, while losers keep falling when analysts underreact more to bad news. Finally, the good-minus-bad volatility effect concentrates among pessimistically tilted, underpriced firms. Overall, belief updating in financial markets is biased differently after good and bad news.

detail.abstract: We examine whether agreement among analysts’ signals has real effects on executives’ compensation-related risk-bearing decisions. Stock option exercises reveal executives’ willingness to bear such risk: exercising converts risky options into value, whereas waiting preserves exposure to future gains and losses. We find that executives are more willing to continue holding options when analysts’ earnings forecasts are tightly aligned and the firm’s valuation path is unstable. The effect is economically large, corresponding to a 24% to 28% reduction in option-implied relative risk aversion. The relation is concentrated among executives with high access to information, which is inconsistent with analyst agreement substituting for private information gaps. Lower relative risk aversion in the studied setting is not associated with superior execution gains and persists after controlling for realized analyst forecast accuracy, inconsistent with superior private information. The relation is concentrated in the pre-crisis period when agreement was later proved optimistic relative to realized earnings, and is stronger in weak-governance firms. Together, our findings show that apparent analyst agreement can shape executives’ compensation-related risk bearing even when analyst signals are not fully validated by subsequent outcomes.

detail.title: Financially Constrained Cities and Commercial Real Estate Returns

detail.abstract: The capitalization of municipal fiscal health into house prices has been widely studied, but commercial real estate (CRE) offers a unique opportunity to examine this relationship without household mobility frictions. We investigate how municipal financial health influences CRE investment performance using data from the Stanford Municipal Finance Dashboard and NCREIF property returns across 90 large U.S. metropolitan areas from 2017 to 2024. We employ panel regressions and a stacked difference-in-differences design exploiting staggered state adoption of fiscal monitoring policies. We find that municipal fiscal health positively predicts CRE returns, with effects operating primarily through appreciation rather than income returns, suggesting investors price fiscal conditions through risk premia and expectations rather than immediate cash flow effects. A one standard deviation improvement in fiscal health is associated with approximately 0.28 percentage points higher quarterly returns (1.1% annually), and enhanced fiscal oversight produces a discrete increase in returns following adoption. Public commercial real estate (CRE) firms with greater portfolio exposure to newly monitored markets earn higher excess returns and increase property acquisitions in those markets, evidence of a capital reallocation margin operating alongside repricing. These findings demonstrate that municipal balance-sheet conditions represent a priced risk factor in commercial real estate markets, with implications for both investors assessing local market exposure and policymakers considering fiscal discipline's spillover effects on private capital formation.

title: Market Efficiency in Prediction Markets: A Multi-Event Analysis of Kalshi Fed Policy Decision Contracts
affiliations: Marquette University

detail.title: Market Efficiency in Prediction Markets: A Multi-Event Analysis of Kalshi Fed Policy Decision Contracts

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I have no personal or financial relationship with other people or organizations that may have or could be perceived to have influenced this study.
declarations.funderStatement: Self-funded.

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether prediction markets function as genuine information-aggregation and risk-pricing mechanisms by analyzing eight settled Federal Reserve interest rate decision contracts traded on Kalshi between September 2025 and July 2026. Using daily price data (691 total observations), we implement a three-part empirical framework: (1) arbitrage spread analysis to evaluate market efficiency, (2) convergence analysis to examine how spreads evolve toward resolution, and (3) event studies to identify the real-world catalysts driving price movements. Our findings reveal three key results. First, market efficiency improves substantially over time as the mean arbitrage spread declined from +5.24 cents (September 2025) to-0.33 cents (July 2026), and a t-test confirms this difference is statistically significant (p < 0.001). Second, prediction markets price differently during cutting versus holding cycles with the mean spread during the 2025 cutting cycle (+2.39 cents) differing significantly from the 2026 holding cycle (-1.07 cents), which suggests that policy regimes affect market pricing behavior. Third, we document extreme pricing discrepancies in early-stage markets, with the June 2026 contract showing the largest standard deviation (7.20) and widest range (-39.75 to +32.00). These extreme spreads are driven by a combination of low liquidity and event-specific uncertainty, and a regression analysis confirms that spreads narrow significantly as resolution approaches (β =-0.008, p < 0.001). Our event study analysis links major price moves to specific macroeconomic catalysts, including CPI releases and Federal Reserve speeches, confirming that these contracts respond to the same fundamental drivers as traditional Treasury and Fed funds futures. This study contributes empirical evidence on market maturation, regime-specific pricing behavior, and the limits to arbitrage in prediction markets. We conclude that while Kalshi Fed decision contracts exhibit strong information-aggregation properties, they also reveal important liquidity constraints and limits to arbitrage that are critical for understanding prediction markets as financial instruments.

detail.title: Survival, Not Growth: Choosing the Exponent in Power-Law Drawdown-Modulated Position Sizing

detail.abstract: Drawdown-constrained position sizing is standard practice in systematic trading, and the continuous-time theory is mature. Grossman and Zhou (1993) show that under geometric Brownian motion, log utility, and frictionless continuous rebalancing, optimal allocation is proportional to the cushion between wealth and a floor set at a fixed fraction of the running maximum. Implementations, however, routinely use power-law variants with exponents chosen by convention rather than derivation. We embed the cushion-proportional rule in a one-parameter family, of which Grossman-Zhou is a special case, and study how the optimal exponent depends on the strategy being controlled. Four results follow. First, the binding consideration is survival rather than growth: over much of the practical range the growth-optimal exponent equals the smallest exponent that avoids terminating the strategy. Second, the survival boundary depends only on strategy volatility relative to the barrier, and is invariant to the barrier level across a sixfold range. Third, a multiplicative controller reaching exactly zero exposure creates an absorbing state in a frictionless market, since zero exposure freezes wealth and therefore freezes drawdown; recoveryband hysteresis is unreachable. Fourth, under sufficiently heavy tails no exponent satisfies the constraint. Results are established by simulation and confirmed on twenty-two years of daily data.

detail.title: Towards Sustainable Development Goal 6: Comparative Evidence on WASH Service Performance Across University-Managed and Private Student Accommodation Systems at the University of Cape Coast, Ghana
detail.abstract: Achieving Sustainable Development Goal 6 requires equitable and reliable water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) services, yet differences in service performance across student-accommodation systems remain poorly understood in sub-Saharan Africa. This study compared reported WASH service performance among students living in university-managed halls and private hostels at the University of Cape Coast, Ghana. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 1,000 students, comprising 500 residents from each accommodation system. A structured questionnaire assessed water availability and appearance, sanitation adequacy and accessibility, cleaning and maintenance, waste management, and perceived health safety. Descriptive statistics, chi-square and Mann–Whitney U tests with effect sizes, and multivariable logistic regression were used to compare accommodation systems. University-managed halls showed less favorable reported water and sanitation outcomes. Water was unavailable daily for 39.4% of hall residents compared with 21.4% of hostel residents, and colored water was reported by 50.8% and 27.8%, respectively. Hall residents experienced greater toilet sharing, less accessible sanitation, lower facility adequacy, less frequent cleaning, and higher perceived health risks than hostel residents, who faced issues with refuse burning and lack of waste collection. After adjusting for age, gender, and duration of residence, hall residents had significantly higher odds of toilet sharing (6.02), perceived health risks (3.16), and rating toilet facilities as inadequate (2.39). Mixed student-accommodation systems can create varied WASH service-performance profiles. Effective monitoring, maintenance, waste management, and accountability can promote equitable and sustainable WASH services, aiding progress toward Sustainable Development Goal 6.

detail.abstract: We develop Entropic Value-at-Risk (EVaR) parity for tempered stable returns. EVaR-based inverse risk parity (IRP) and equal risk contribution (ERC) portfolios are constructed using multivariate normal tempered stable models and independent component analysis with tempered stable components. We derive the corresponding asset-level EVaR and EVaR-deviation contributions and use the latter to separate the tted location term from EVaR risk contributions. Under Gaussian returns, EVaR-deviation IRP and ERC recover conventional volatility IRP and ERC weights. We evaluate the resulting portfolios in three investment universes. Empirically, EVaR-based ERC portfolios achieve positive Sharpe dierences relative to equal weight across the universes.

detail.abstract: A liquidity constraint can shut down the transaction designed to relieve it. Ginnie Mae issuers must advance principal and interest on non-paying loans; the early buyout-repurchasing a delinquent loan at par—is the only contractual escape, and exercising it consumes the balance sheet the obligation drains. Using 3.1 million option-exercise decisions across 385 issuers, I show that when the COVID-19 liquidity shock arrived, nonbank buyout rates fell from 45% to 10% while depository rates rose from 80% to 92%. The nonbank decline is largest on the highest-coupon loans, where the trade is most valuable—the signature of a binding financing constraint, not a change in the option’s worth. Which servicing regime a distressed household entered was determined by the funding structure of whoever held its servicing.

detail.abstract: Under the Internal Revenue Code, foreign persons engaged in a trade or business in the United States are generally subject to U.S. net basis taxation on their income that is effectively connected with the U.S. business, otherwise known as "effectively connected income" or "ECI." The general policy underlying the ECI rules is to tax foreign persons on income that is derived from U.S. business activities. For the most part, these rules do a decent job in capturing income that is generated by a foreign person's U.S. business. However, for certain transactions, including sales of inventory, the ECI rules fail to accurately determine U.S. business income because of two features: (i) the "U.S. office or other fixed place of business" ("USFPB") requirement and (ii) the residual force of attraction rule. The USFPB requirement results in under-inclusions of a foreign person's U.S. business income, while the residual force of attraction rule causes over-inclusions. For these and other reasons, this Article recommends the elimination of the USFPB requirement for determining the ECI status and source of certain income, as well as the elimination of the residual force of attraction rule. With these reforms, the ECI rules will more accurately capture income that is generated by the U.S. business activities of foreign persons.

Using survey data from a representative sample of more than 3,000 French adult internet users, we find that social media use is strongly associated with digital addiction and that responsiveness to dark patterns is positively related to multiple measures of addictive online behavior. detail.abstract: We study government disclosure of the spatial distribution of climate risk. A regulator decides whether to reveal which region is exposed to disaster risk. Households can insure against the disaster or relocate at a cost. Disclosure induces migration out of the risky region, which reduces aggregate risk but impairs risk sharing by revealing who is exposed. Migration also lowers insurance prices by increasing the supply of and decreasing the demand for insurance. With sufficient relocation, disclosure can be Pareto improving. Unlimited ex-post disaster relief eliminates relocation, and with it the value of disclosure. A capped relief fund preserves some relocation while restoring some risk sharing, making disclosure and relief complements.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates the joint dynamics of market liquidity, high-frequency trading (HFT) activity, corporate bond pricing, and mutual fund flow volatility in the U.S. corporate bond market over the period 2003 to 2023. Using a comprehensive dataset drawn from FINRA’s Enhanced TRACE, the CRSP Mutual Fund Database, Mergent FISD, and TAQ intraday records, we construct fund-level and bond-level measures of liquidity, HFT intensity, and price impact. Our core empirical finding is that elevated HFT activity in corporate bond markets systematically compresses bid-ask spreads and reduces the Amihud price-impact measure during normal market conditions, yet amplifies intraday price volatility and fund-flow sensitivity during stress episodes. We document that mutual funds holding portfolios of less liquid bonds exhibit sharper flow-performance concavity, consistent with strategic redemption complementarities under illiquidity. Moreover, we show that the moderating role of HFT on liquidity provision reverses during market dislocations — most prominently during the Global Financial Crisis (2008–2009), the Taper Tantrum (2013), and the COVID-19 Dash-for-Cash (March 2020) — when HFT withdrawal amplifies spreads and price dislocations. Cross-sectional analyses reveal that funds with higher portfolio illiquidity exhibit larger return reversals and greater sensitivity of outflows to adverse performance shocks.

title: Information-Filtration Trade-off in Thompson Sampling for MNL Bandits
affiliations: and University of Chile - Industrial Engineering

detail.title: Information-Filtration Trade-off in Thompson Sampling for MNL Bandits
detail.abstract: Dynamic assortment learning under multinomial logit (MNL) demand couples revenue and information through the denominator shared by every displayed product, which fixes what an assortment earns and what each choice reveals. We study Thompson sampling, where every decision optimizes an attraction vector drawn from the representation it maintains. That representation is a design choice: filtering the likelihood to product-versus-outside comparisons gives one conjugate law per product but discards the substitution evidence coupling the attractions, which the complete likelihood keeps at a cost. We analyze both ends of this information-filtration trade-off, and one approximation in between. At the filtered end, the probability that several independent draws are optimistic at once can decay exponentially in the display capacity K; existing analyses avoid this by correlating, resampling, or inflating draws. None of that is necessary: the linear-fractional form of MNL revenue tests whether correcting one omitted draw would improve the sampled optimum; with scalar posterior odds and per-product clocks, coordinate repair gives gap-free frequentist regret Õ(√(NKT)) for independent BetaPrime draws, without resampling or variance inflation. At the complete end, a Gamma–Exponential augmentation yields a Gibbs sampler for the joint posterior, and exact draws from it attain Bayesian regret Õ(√(NT)), uniformly in K. These appear to be the first such guarantees for product-wise independent draws and the complete MNL posterior. A mean-field representation attains the same rate once its dispersion is corrected for the coupling it discards; a computational study maps the statistical–computational trade-off.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates the systemic funding liquidity risk in fixed-income portfolios, particularly during periods of macroeconomic downturns. We develop a robust modeling framework to identify and quantify the impact of liquidity shocks across various fixed-income asset classes. Utilizing a combination of econometric techniques and machine learning algorithms, our approach aims to capture the non-linear dynamics and interconnectedness within financial markets. The findings provide critical insights for risk managers, policymakers, and institutional investors in developing more resilient portfolio strategies and enhancing financial stability. We demonstrate the utility of our model through case studies of historical downturns, highlighting key transmission channels and vulnerabilities. Our framework further contributes to the literature by bridging traditional macroeconomic stress testing with modern predictive analytics. Unlike conventional models that treat liquidity as exogenous, we endogenize funding liquidity as a dynamic variable driven by market sentiment, monetary policy shifts, and balance sheet constraints. By combining Vector Autoregression (VAR) for impulse response analysis with Random Forest classifiers for early warning signals, the model offers both explanatory power and practical forecasting capability. This dual approach allows institutions to not only understand how liquidity shocks propagate during downturns but also to anticipate and mitigate them before they materialize into systemic events.

detail.abstract:
This study determined the effect of exchange rate volatility on the gross margins of listed Nigerian manufacturing firms and examined the effect of the exchange rate volatility on the gross margins of listed banks, It also compared and contrasted the magnitude, direction, and statistical significance of the volatility–gross-margin relationship between the manufacturing and banking sectors.

The study employed an ex post facto and longitudinal research design. A panel of twenty firms listed on the Nigerian Exchange Group consisting of ten banks and ten manufacturing companies was observed annually from 2015 to 2025. Exchange rate volatility was measured using the conditional variance from a GARCH(1,1) model fitted to daily Naira/US Dollar returns. Firm‑level financial data were extracted from audited annual reports. Three Fixed Effects panel regression models were estimated, with robustness assessed through cluster‑robust standard errors, panel unit root tests, cross‑sectional dependence diagnostics, and Hausman specification tests. All analyses were conducted in Gretl and R.

The findings show that exchange rate volatility has a negative and statistically significant effect on bank gross‑earnings margins, robust to cluster‑robust correction. For manufacturing firms, the coefficient is also negative but not significant at the 5 % level. The interaction term testing for cross‑sector difference is not significant. 

The study concluded that banking's negative relationship with exchange rate volatility shows that the credit quality channel and funding cost dominate the gains from  foreign currency revaluation. The weak manufacturing significance likely reflects sub‑sector heterogeneity or the mitigating role of pricing pass-through in some industries.. Recommendations are advanced for corporate treasurers, bank risk managers, and policymakers, with exchange rate stability identified as a cross‑cutting macroeconomic priority.

detail.abstract: Conventional spacecraft are organized around launch-vehicle geometry, onboard propellant, and a single dominant propulsion system. Those choices make missions highly dependent on the rocket equation, narrow launch windows, destination specific stages, and limited braking options. This conceptual design study asks a deliberately radical but physics-bounded question: what would a spacecraft look like if it were designed primarily for travel in space rather than for ascent through an atmosphere? The proposed Asterion architecture replaces the familiar rocket shaped vehicle with a distributed annular craft whose propulsion is field-coupled and multi-regime. It combines externally supplied photon or pellet-beam momentum, deployable solar and electric sails, a plasma-inflated magnetic sail, optional fission- or fusion-electric onboard power, destination-side braking, high temperature radiator petals, replaceable forward shielding, autonomous reconfiguration, and in-space assembly. A separate spacetime-metric laboratory branch is retained only as a fundamental-physics experiment and contributes no credited mission performance. Governing equations for beam thrust, heat rejection, charged-particle deflection, and relativistic impact energy are used to expose the design’s dominant constraints. An illustrative 1,000 kg probe accelerated by a 100 GW idealized reflected beam with 85% effective momentum coupling would experience approximately 567 N, reaching 300 km/s in about 6.1 days over roughly 0.53 AU, while simultaneously creating severe optical, structural, pointing, and thermal challenges. The study concludes that the most defensible path to radically improved mobility is not a single “impossible engine,” but an infrastructure supported vehicle that changes propulsion mode with environment and mission phase. The paper defines evidence gates, failure modes, and a staged demonstration roadmap intended to prevent speculative elements from being confused with engineering readiness.

detail.abstract: Contemporary organizations increasingly comprise employees from multiple generations working within the same departments, creating opportunities for knowledge exchange, diverse perspectives, and collective learning. At the same time, differences in communication preferences, work expectations, values, and interpretations of professional responsibility may create challenges for collaboration. This study explores how multiple generations coexist within organizational departments and examines the organizational conditions that influence collaboration, conflict, commitment, and performance. A qualitative multiple-case study design was employed, involving two private-sector organizational departments: one within a large, highly structured organization and one within a medium-sized organization characterized by a less formalized environment. Data were collected through semistructured interviews with two departmental managers and six employees representing different generational cohorts. The findings indicate that although participants perceived generational differences as influencing workplace interactions, these differences did not independently determine organizational outcomes. Instead, leadership practices, organizational culture, accountability mechanisms, and communication structures shaped how generational diversity was experienced and managed. In the large organization, clear expectations, consistent managerial involvement, timely conflict resolution, and open communication supported cooperation and minimized interpersonal tensions. In contrast, limited managerial intervention and inconsistent reinforcement of behavioral expectations in the medium-sized organization contributed to unresolved conflict, reduced accountability, and declining team cohesion. The findings further suggest that behaviors commonly attributed to generational characteristics may instead reflect broader organizational influences, including changing psychological contracts and evolving expectations regarding work, fairness, development, and organizational support. By shifting attention from generational categories to the organizational context in which employees work, this study offers a more contextualized understanding of multigenerational coexistence and highlights the central role of leadership and organizational practices in fostering effective collaboration across generations.

detail.abstract: Major capital projects are increasingly delivered with sophisticated project management, engineering, commissioning, and governance practices, yet successful project delivery does not consistently translate into sustained operational performance. Delayed ramp-up, operational instability, safety exposure, and value erosion frequently emerge after technical completion, revealing a persistent gap between project success and the organizational capability required to operate assets effectively under real conditions. This paper proposes a unified conceptualization of Operational Readiness as a dynamic organizational capability rather than a project phase, checklist, or collection of transition activities. Building on Dynamic Capabilities theory and a systems perspective of organizations, the paper introduces a two-dimensional model of Operational Readiness. The Structural Dimension identifies four interdependent Core Capabilities: People, Systems & Processes, Organization, and Assets, through which readiness resides and is developed. The Developmental Dimension explains how these capabilities progressively mature through three states: Awareness, Preparedness, and Readiness, toward the demonstrated ability to assume operational responsibility with confidence. The model reframes traditional readiness activities such as commissioning, organizational change, risk management, asset management, governance, and operational planning as complementary mechanisms for developing a broader organizational capability. It also distinguishes technical completion from true readiness by shifting attention from the completion of activities and deliverables toward the organization’s ability to absorb uncertainty, adapt to operational realities, and sustain safe, reliable, and value-generating performance. The paper concludes that Operational Readiness can provide an integrative conceptual foundation for advancing professional practice, readiness assessment, governance, resilience, and value realization across complex capital-project environments.

detail.abstract: The international textile and apparel sector faces an unprecedented structural reckoning driven by accelerating ecological degradation, systemic data inventory fragmentation, and non-discretionary cross-border regulatory frameworks. Generating approximately 10% of global carbon emissions and over 1.45 million tonnes of annual domestic used waste in individual regions like the UK, the "linear fast fashion economy" is hit by newly enacted constraints. Chief among these is the European Union's Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR) destruction ban on unsold textiles, which came into direct enforcement on 19 July 2026, alongside the structural development of the EU Digital Product Passport (DPP) registry infrastructure. This paper analyzes the macro-level operational gap created by these regulations. While enterprise retailers possess the financial reserves to adjust their master supply chains, independent Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) face contract cancellations due to a "cascading procurement burden." SMEs manage inventory records via unstandardized, disconnected text registries, preventing the item-level fiber verification that downstream enterprise distributors now legally require to insulate themselves from massive environmental penalties. This study reviews the material composition crises, mapping data anomalies, and the critical path required to shift industrial practices from high-overhead physical asset accumulation to programmatic data routing layers, outlining the structural necessity for localized, entry-level compliance pipelines.

detail.abstract: Master data has become a critical foundation for how large enterprises coordinate operations, ensure consistency, and maintain confidence in business information across organizational boundaries. As enterprises expand across regions, product lines, and regulatory jurisdictions, the volume and complexity of shared business entities such as customers, products, counterparties, and reference attributes increase significantly. These shared entities are reused across transactional systems, analytical platforms, and reporting structures, making their accuracy and consistency central to enterprise performance. Master data management emerges in this context not as a discrete technical solution, but as a discipline that governs how core business information is defined, controlled, and sustained across the enterprise landscape. Despite widespread investment in enterprise systems, many organizations continue to struggle with fragmented master data ownership and inconsistent definitions across business domains.

detail.abstract: Cost-benefit analysis begins with a natural question: what must be given up, and what might be gained? Its historical achievement was to turn that ordinary logic into a portable technology of public decision. This paper reconstructs that achievement as a succession of reasonable reductions. Political arithmetic made society numerically legible. Bentham made consequences aggregable. Dupuit translated the utility of public works into monetary equivalents. Marginalism supplied a mathematical language of scalar value, local change and equilibrium. Welfare economics addressed winners and losers. Discounting placed different times on one present scale. Public agencies made the method repeatable. Herbert Simon explained why bounded human and organisational reason requires such simplification. Robert McNamara then carried a cognate quantified style of management from Ford and the Pentagon into the World Bank, where project appraisal, shadow pricing and rates of return acquired global institutional authority. The achievement was real. So was the compression. Cost-benefit analysis is rigorous only within a domain in which boundaries remain serviceable, effects remain sufficiently separable, monetary translation remains reasonably stable and the intervention does not reconstruct the possibility space itself. The paper therefore neither rejects CBA nor permits its scalar result to govern without qualification. It restores CBA to its proper place as a late-stage, conditional measurement within a larger appraisal of an adaptive human world.

detail.abstract: We explore the effect of intellectual property (IP) boxes on the nature of firms' innovative activities. As a policy tool to stimulate innovation, IP boxes offer a reduced tax rate on income generated from patents and other IP investments. We examine how IP box tax incentives affect firms' production of basic research (i.e., scientific publications) and commercially marketable research (i.e., patents). Using a European crosscountry setting and a stacked cohort difference-indifferences design, we find that IP box adoption is associated with a decrease in scientific publications and an increase in patents over the next three to five years, suggesting a trade-off between publishing and patenting activities. Results are strongest among financially constrained firms, in tight labor markets, and in IP box regimes with greater benefits. Additionally, while non-patent-related publications decline, publications receive more patent citations, and both radical and incremental patents increase post-IP box adoption. Finally, using individual-level author and inventor data, we find that the same individuals reduce publishing and increase patenting after IP box adoption. Our results are robust to using multiple subsamples and horizons. Our findings suggest that tax incentives that reward successful innovation motivate firms to direct resources away from publishing and toward patenting.

detail.abstract:
Canonical wealth theory is built on an idealized holder: an agent that averages across
parallel outcomes, values everything in one unit, can reverse its losses, and never dies.
Existential Portfolio Theory begins instead from a finite, singular, embodied holder,
valuing plural goods that resist a common measure, and follows the consequences. On
these foundations, wealth becomes a configuration in time rather than a quantity: a
portfolio of heterogeneous, partially convertible capitals whose outcome depends not
only on levels but on sequence. The theory’s central result, the sequencing thesis, holds
that two holders identical in endowments can diverge into viable and collapsed trajec-
tories by order alone. From the same foundations it derives that ruin-avoidance takes
priority over return-seeking; that no single number can represent a holder’s wealth
without destroying the information that matters; and that stewardship — custodial,
downside-first, regeneration-respecting governance of the whole configuration — is not
a moral preference but what rational management becomes when the theory licenses
no global maximand, when ensemble expectations cannot stand in for the one trajectory
actually lived, and when there is no second life on which to apply what ruin teaches.
The theory states what would count against it, and is offered openly for exactly that
purpose.

title: Which Contract: Caste and the Form of Tenancy in Rural India

detail.title: Which Contract: Caste and the Form of Tenancy in Rural India

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests. No party with a stake in the findings had any role in the design, analysis, or reporting of this study.
declarations.funderStatement: The author is supported by a Junior Research Fellowship from the [University Grants Commission / Council of Scientific and Industrial Research / Indian Council of Social Science Research]. The fellowship is stipendiary doctoral support and was not awarded for this project. The funder had no role in the design, analysis, or reporting of the study. No other funding was received.

detail.abstract:
Caste decides which tenancy contract a rural household gets. Rural tenancy takes two
priced forms. Under a fixed rent the tenant pays the landlord a set amount and keeps
whatever else he grows. Under a share of produce he hands over a fixed fraction of the
harvest, almost always one half, so he keeps only half of anything extra he produces.
In the two National Sample Survey rounds that record tenancy plot by plot, a Scheduled
Caste tenant is more likely than a general caste tenant in the same district to hold his land
on a share rather than a fixed rent: 6.9 percentage points in 2003 (p = .009) and 14.9
points in 2013 (p = .011). Sharecropping runs General below Other Backward Class
below Scheduled Caste in both rounds and on either way of counting the leases, though only
the Scheduled Caste step is statistically established. The point estimate is larger in 2013,
but the two rounds cannot be told apart (+8.1 points, p = .21), so the paper reports the
difference in both rounds and claims no path over time.
There is a reason to doubt that finding, and the paper tests it. Almost all tenancy here
is oral, and many leases reach the survey with no terms recorded at all; these go into a third
category, land held from relatives on no stated terms. Perhaps Scheduled Caste leases are
only written up more precisely, so that what looks like more sharecropping is really better
paperwork. If that were so, Scheduled Caste tenants would hold fewer no-terms leases. They
do not. In both rounds, Scheduled Caste and general caste tenants living in the same district
hold no-terms leases at about the same rate.
The same gap appears in a third and unrelated survey, the India Human Development
Survey, and it survives controls for the household’s owned land and, nationally, its livestock.
A village survey, the Rural Economic and Demographic Survey of 2005-06, records the
size of the share as well as its form, and adds two things. Within the village, where tenants
face the same land and the same rental customs, the gap is 28 points. And the price has
almost no room to move, because it is a convention: 79 percent of sharecropped parcels
owe exactly one half of output, and 3 percent owe more. Compared like for like at state
resolution, a 21 point gap in assignment sits against a share coefficient of +0.001.
Caste in this market works on which contract a household holds, not on what that
contract charges. The estimates are conditional associations in repeated cross sections. They
describe a market, not any lessor’s decision rule.

detail.abstract: Prompted by the United States Supreme Court's decision in Trump v. Cook (2026), this article examines the constitutional position of the Bank of England within the United Kingdom's uncodified constitution. The article traces the Bank's development from its foundation in 1694 through nationalisation in 1946 and the grant of operational independence in 1997-98, showing how its constitutional significance has emerged through historical practice as well as statutory design. It argues that the Bank's enduring legal personality, sustained for more than 330 years, means that it does not merely exist within the constitution; it has become part of the constitutional fabric of the state itself. In particular, it argues that the Bank occupies a constitutionally distinctive place within the executive, as an institution of long historical standing, entrusted by Parliament with the exercise of independent expert judgement in safeguarding the value of the currency and maintaining the financial stability, while remaining accountable to Parliament and ultimately subject to the principle of parliamentary sovereignty. It argues that there is a good case that the Bank of England Act 1998 bears the hallmarks of a constitutional statute, structuring the relationship between Parliament, government and the central bank. Finally, it develops a constitutional analogy between the Bank and the judiciary: institutions entrusted with the exercise of specialised expertise and independent judgement, protected from improper political interference, yet accountable within a constitutional framework ultimately established by Parliament.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the concept of the "blue economy" as a strategic approach for the sustainable use of ocean and sea resources to promote economic growth, social well-being, and environmental sustainability. Particular emphasis is placed on the link between the blue economy and food security, especially in the context of coastal cities that depend on marine resources for food and income. Key challenges are described, including pollution, climate change, overfishing, and degradation of marine ecosystems. Solutions are proposed through sustainable fishing, development of responsible aquaculture, innovative marine technologies, and maritime spatial planning. The emphasis is on implementing environmental and management innovations to ensure the long-term stability of marine ecosystems and sustainable access to seafood. The European Union plays a key role in this transition through policies such as the "Green Deal", the "Blue Growth" strategy, and mechanisms for the greening of the maritime economy. Bulgaria is actively involved through programmes for sustainable aquaculture, maritime spatial planning, and the fight against illegal fishing, especially in the Black Sea region. The article highlights the need for an interdisciplinary and international approach based on scientific evidence and sustainable policies. The conclusion is that the blue economy is not just an economic concept, but an integrated strategy for the future of coastal societies and global food security.

detail.abstract:
The conflict between the Ossetian and Ingush ethnic groups had severe political consequences. Although the reconciliation process has been ongoing for more than two decades, its results remain questionable. The Russian Federation has played a decisive role throughout both the conflict and the subsequent reconciliation process. The Russian authorities treated the Ingush side unequally while supporting the Ossetians; this approach contributed to the escalation of the conflict and subsequently created obstacles to effective mediation and dialogue.

This article examines the scope and effectiveness of intergovernmental agreements by analyzing relations among the Ossetian, Ingush, and Russian authorities. It identifies a broader set of political factors that have shaped societal attitudes among the conflicting parties. The study also seeks to identify some of the key factors that determined the Kremlin’s position during both the conflict and the reconciliation process.

detail.abstract: Social programs designed to help disadvantaged groups typically direct resources and attention to that group alone: when a targeted disadvantage is sustained by the group's broader social environment, excluding that social environment from the program may itself affects how it responds. We test this using a cluster-randomized controlled trial across 52 schools in Nepal, randomly varying whether boys are included alongside girls in a menstrual health awareness session designed to reduce stigma. Boys who are excluded from the session become 17 percent less likely to commit to speaking up against menstrual stigma, relative to boys that receive no session at all; including boys offsets this decline. This response operates through both social an internal channels: exclusion lowers boys' expectations of peer support for challenging menstrual stigma, and weakens their own connection to the issue.

detail.abstract: Since employment dynamics are persistent, a central bank's dual mandate to promote maximum employment and price stability naturally generates history dependence in monetary policy. This history dependence under a dual mandate flattens the reducedform Phillips curve, reduces the volatility of inflation in response to demand shocks, and improves outcomes at the zero lower bound. Moreover, we show that a dual mandate can be observationally equivalent to average inflation targeting following a demand shock. However, this equivalence breaks down in the presence of supply shocks. We first illustrate these findings analytically and then examine their quantitative importance in a model with nominal rigidities and labor search frictions calibrated to match U.S. business-cycle moments. An employment mandate can naturally provide the stabilization benefits associated with history-dependent policy frameworks.

title: Activation without diffusion:   Sequential investment and diffusion barriers in shared CCS infrastructure under carbon-price uncertainty
affiliations: Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) - Shanghai Advanced Research Institute, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Central South University, Central South University, Tianjin University, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) - Shanghai Advanced Research Institute and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Activation without diffusion:   Sequential investment and diffusion barriers in shared CCS infrastructure under carbon-price uncertainty
detail.abstract: Carbon capture and storage (CCS) hubs are expected to reduce decarbonization costs by allowing multiple emitters to share transport and storage infrastructure. However, making an anchor project investable does not necessarily induce subsequent firms to participate. We investigate this sequential investment problem using a real-options game under carbon-price uncertainty and constrained shared capacity. The framework compares net present value, a single-firm real option, and strategic Leader–Follower investment thresholds, and uses 100,000 Monte Carlo carbon-price paths to evaluate threshold-triggering probabilities over time. In the benchmark case, the NPV break-even carbon price is 245.36 CNY/tCO2, while the single-firm real-option threshold is 731.15 CNY/tCO2. Strategic entry lowers the Leader threshold to 278.34 CNY/tCO2 through pre-emption but raises the Follower threshold to 973.70 CNY/tCO2 as shared-capacity constraints reduce post-entry returns, generating an activation–diffusion gap of 695.35 CNY/tCO2. By 2046, only 7.01% of activated carbon-price pathways progress to Follower entry. More favorable carbon-price pathways with faster growth or wider realized dispersion improve activation-to-entry conversion but remain insufficient for broad diffusion under the benchmark threshold structure. By contrast, capacity reservation, benefit sharing, and differentiated policy support directly reshape investment conditions across entry stages and substantially narrow the gap. An application to the Bohai Bay CCS network further shows that the activation–diffusion mechanism persists in a real-network setting. These results show that the economic success of CCS hubs depends not only on enabling initial activation, but also on aligning infrastructure access and investment returns so that activation can translate into sustained subsequent participation.

detail.abstract: This study investigates the association between entrepreneurs' stress response, anxiety, and depressive symptoms and their innovative thinking during a logistics crisis. Although previous research has examined the effects of stress and anxiety on job performance, employee behavior, business sustainability, and creativity of employees, among other themes, limited attention has been given to the relationship between psychological resources and innovative thinking under conditions of severe logistical disruption. A mixed-methods approach was adopted, using questionnaires and semi-structured interviews with MSME owners and managers. Descriptive findings indicated moderate levels of psychological distress and perceived stress among participants. The mean total HADS score was 19.37 (SD = 2.77), with subscale means of 8.375 (SD = 1.92) for anxiety and 11 (SD = 2.39) for depression, and the mean PSS score was 41 (SD = 10.55). Despite the variability in distress and stress levels across participants, qualitative findings indicated that entrepreneurs continued to develop innovative products, services, and processes and to pursue investment decisions during the logistics crisis. The findings suggest that psychological distress and innovative responses may coexist during crisis conditions. The study contributes to the literature by examining the relationship between entrepreneurs' stress response, anxiety, depression symptoms, and innovative thinking and provides practical implications for supporting entrepreneurial innovation, resource allocation, and business sustainability.

detail.abstract: This paper analyzes the economic and behavioral inefficiencies of GLP-1 medications like Ozempic in the global market. While these drugs help with short-term weight loss , data shows high discontinuation rates reaching 64% within two years. This is followed by a major weight rebound, creating a repeating consumption loop. At the same time, the global market is a strict duopoly controlled by companies in the USA and Denmark, which keeps prices very high. As global obesity rates continue to rise toward an estimated 4 billion people by 2035 , relying heavily on these imported medications creates a permanent drain on national wealth and a state of chronic import dependency. This study demonstrates these inefficiencies and argues for a policy shift toward domestic, service-based health solutions instead of foreign products.

detail.abstract: Organisations tend to consider AI implementation as a completed process-a tool is selected, reviewed, implemented and governed. However, what looks like a stable product hides ongoing change: the supplier modifies models and capabilities, integration adds access to information, and employees find new use cases that were not considered in the original assessment and approval process. This paper explores reasons behind the fact that a change invalidates previously made organisational decisions without requiring a new implementation project. By synthesising research on situated technological change, learning algorithms, organisational readiness to adopt AI and the automation-augmentation paradox, it develops the concept of organisational re-entry and proposes three propositions about the condition under which it is required and its proportionality. It is argued that an implementation of AI should be considered a provisional organisational settlement rather than a final stage.
