title: Connectome-GPT-Worm - Fine-Tuning a Generative Biologically Trained (GBT) Model: Using the C. elegans Connectome for Language-Based Problems and Large Language Modelling

detail.title: Connectome-GPT-Worm - Fine-Tuning a Generative Biologically Trained (GBT) Model: Using the C. elegans Connectome for Language-Based Problems and Large Language Modelling

declarations.declarationOfInterest: na
declarations.ethicsApproval: na
declarations.funderStatement: na

publicationDetails.detailsText: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22545298 [undefined]

detail.abstract:
I introduce Connectome-GPT-Worm, a Generative Biologically-Pretrained Transformer (GBT) that embeds a fixed, anatomically exact connectome matrix drawn from Caenorhabditis elegans (302 neurons) as both a trainable and a non-trainable intermediate layer inside a GPT-style language model. All remaining weights, from token embedding through encoder and decoder transformer blocks to the language modelling head, are trained from scratch on WikiText-103 via standard next-token prediction.

The biological connectivity acts as a frozen structural prior that learnable components must negotiate; the model must simultaneously learn a projection into neuronal space and an inverse mapping back to linguistic representational space. I add in an "artifact layer", that permits the model to learn the human-to-worm-artifact relationships, the worm-artifact to worm-representation relationships, worm-representation relationships to the worm-artifact representations, and finally work-artifact to human-language representations.  

I present a comprehensive literature fused with a personal scientific anecdotal account of how I arrived at my ideas through my individual struggles from the prior 3 years after suffering from acute academic burnout due to over work committments during the COVID-19 Pandemic.

The review situating this work lies at the intersection of three disciplines: (i)the origin and evolution of artificial neural networks and their biological inspiration; (ii)the use of artificial neural networks as scientific instruments for studying real nervous systems, including connectome-constrained modelling; and (iii)the architecture and training philosophy of modern large language models. I show how these threads converge in the Connectome-GPT-Worm and discuss the theoretical implications, including links to Cartesian Dualist Dogmas, inductive linguistic etymological biases, reservoir computing, spectral stability, and the question of whether structured biological priors can augment or qualitatively reshape learned linguistic representations.  Put simply, do biological connectomes contain sufficient information, if any, to give us a computational edge on language and machine learning problems within artifical intelligence and artificial generative intelligence.

title: Integrating Geriatric Principles into Perioperative Care: A Virtual Geriatric Unit Model with 39‑Month Surveillance and Healthspan Implications
affiliations: Zhengzhou University - Affiliated Zhengzhou Central Hospital, Zhengzhou University - Affiliated Zhengzhou Central Hospital and Zhengzhou University - Zhengzhou Central Hospital

detail.title: Integrating Geriatric Principles into Perioperative Care: A Virtual Geriatric Unit Model with 39‑Month Surveillance and Healthspan Implications

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: The study protocol was approved by the Medical Ethics Committee of Zhengzhou Central Hospital Affiliated to Zhengzhou University (approval number: ZXYY2026198). The committee waived written informed consent due to secondary analysis of anonymised data.
declarations.funderStatement: None.

detail.abstract:
Background: The global rise in surgical volume among older adults has exposed a fundamental mismatch between perioperative care delivery and the needs of an ageing population. Multimorbidity, depleted physiological reserve, and dysregulated stress responses amplify vulnerability to postoperative complications. Conventional models systematically miss geriatric syndromes; the "virtual ward" construct offers a proactive alternative, yet its implementation across the full perioperative arc remains incompletely evaluated.

Methods: This quasi‑experimental study used the July 2022 launch of a "Virtual Geriatric Unit—Surgery (VGUs)" as the intervention breakpoint in 11,642 older inpatients (median age 74 years) undergoing grade III/IV procedures, with surveillance through January 2026. Segmented regression with interrupted time series estimated intervention effects; Firth‑penalised logistic regression identified factors associated with complications. External validation was performed in eICU‑CRI and MIMIC‑IV. Exploratory biomarker analyses examined inflammatory and functional pathways.

Findings: VGUs implementation was associated with an immediate 5.21 percentage‑point complication reduction (95% CI: −8.92 to −1.50; P = 0.012) and a monthly decline of 0.89 percentage points (95% CI: −1.52 to −0.26; P = 0.009). Rates remained ≤1.1% through January 2026—39 months of sustained low levels. CGA completion rose from 42.8% to 98.6%. Length of stay fell by 4.1 days, cost per admission by RMB 18,000. ASA grade ≥ III (OR = 2.87), emergency surgery (OR = 3.52), ≥3 comorbidities (OR = 1.98), and frailty (OR = 2.21) emerged as independent risk factors; prehabilitation was protective (OR = 0.51). External validation confirmed these associations (pooled OR: 2.84, 3.48, 1.96, and 2.18; all I² = 0%).

Interpretation: In this large real‑world cohort with 39‑month surveillance and external validation, a VGUs model was associated with sustained reductions in complications, hospital stays, and costs—benefits that persisted for more than three years. Attenuated inflammation and preserved physical function may link the intervention to healthspan preservation. These findings suggest that integrating geriatric principles into perioperative care can mitigate the amplified vulnerability that defines ageing surgical patients, with potential implications for healthy longevity.

title: Effort-Independent Preoperative Pulmonary Function Assessment Using CT-Based Deep Learning to Guide Surgical Decision-Making: A Retrospective, Multicentre, External Validation Study

detail.title: Effort-Independent Preoperative Pulmonary Function Assessment Using CT-Based Deep Learning to Guide Surgical Decision-Making: A Retrospective, Multicentre, External Validation Study

declarations.declarationOfInterest: We declare no competing interests.

The requirement for individual informed consent was waived by the ethics committee due to the retrospective design and the use of anonymized routinely collected clinical data.
declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported by the National Key Research and Development Program of China (Grant No. 2023YFC2508601), the National Natural Science Foundation of China (Grant No. 82572991), and the Guangdong Basic and Applied Basic Research Foundation (Grant No. 2025A1515010570).

detail.abstract:
Background: Accurate preoperative pulmonary function assessment is essential for surgical risk stratification and decision-making in thoracic surgery. However, conventional spirometry is inherently effort-dependent and often unfeasible for patients unable to perform reliable maneuvers due to acute pain, respiratory distress, or poor compliance. We aimed to develop and externally validate a computed tomography (CT)-based multimodal deep learning framework (NF-Co-ViT) to provide effort-independent pulmonary function estimates directly from chest CT scans.

Methods: In this retrospective, multicentre study, we evaluated 2,188 patients undergoing thoracic surgery with paired chest CT and spirometry across four independent cohorts. The NF-Co-ViT model was trained and internally cross-validated on the primary cohort (n = 1,835) and externally validated on three independent multicentre cohorts (n = 353). By mapping volumetric CT representations into an invertible normative latent space, the model quantifies functional deficits through latent space residuals relative to physiological norms. Primary outcomes were predictive errors for forced vital capacity (FVC) and forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1). Secondary outcomes assessed model discrimination across clinically relevant decision thresholds for surgical eligibility and resection extent (FEV1/FVC > 70%, FEV1% > 80%, and FEV1 > 2.0 L).

Findings: In the external validation, the model achieved a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.081 L for both FVC and FEV1, demonstrating strong agreement with standard spirometry (Pearson correlation coefficient [r] ≥ 0.992 and intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC] ≥ 0.992). For identifying critical clinical cutoffs, the model yielded areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.964 for FEV1/FVC > 70%, 0.990 for FEV1% > 80% (measured FEV1 value/predicted FEV1 value), and 0.993 for FEV1 > 2.0 L.

Interpretation: By replacing unconstrained deep regression with a normative reference space mapping, NF-Co-ViT bridges statistical deep learning representations with established pathophysiological reasoning. This CT-based framework enables accurate, effort-independent estimation of preoperative pulmonary function, offering a practical non-invasive surrogate to support preoperative risk evaluation and surgical decision-making.

title: Childcare for Informal-Sector Workers: Delivery Models, Access, and Welfare
affiliations: , Ace Policy Research Institute, , World Bank, World Bank’s Development Research Group,  and World Bank

detail.title: Childcare for Informal-Sector Workers: Delivery Models, Access, and Welfare
detail.abstract: Childcare burdens limit productivity among women in the informal sector, but we know little about the optimal design of childcare support. We randomize 883 women market vendors in Kampala, Uganda to receive free workplace- or community-based childcare. Free childcare redistributes caregiving away from household members, raises women’s hourly earnings, and improves child development and women’s well-being. Community centers achieve higher utilization and larger gains in development and well-being, while workplace centers generate larger economic impacts. Both models have a high marginal value of public funds. Community centers currently dominate, but workplace-based centers could prove superior if operated at scale.

title: The Costs and Benefits of Mediocrity: Endogenous Auction Design in Procurement
affiliations: University of Tübingen - Department of Economics and Tübingen University

detail.title: The Costs and Benefits of Mediocrity: Endogenous Auction Design in Procurement
detail.abstract: We study bidding in a broad class of price-based procurement mechanisms in which the lowest bid does not always win. These mechanisms are used when cost overruns and non-compliance affect contract execution. We first characterize equilibrium bidding behavior in a general setting with endogenous winning probabilities. We then analyze mixed auction formats in which bidders face uncertainty about the allocation rule, as in the Italian system where a lowest-price or average bid rule is selected based on participation. We show that increasing reliance on the latter can improve compliance but raises bids and expected payments, highlighting a trade-off between contract performance and low award prices.

title: Zero-Shot Conditional Forecasting and the Information Content of Central Bank Paths
affiliations: BI Norwegian Business School, Department of Data Science and Analytics and Centre for Applied Macroeconomics and Commodity Prices (CAMP), BI Norwegian Business School

detail.title: Zero-Shot Conditional Forecasting and the Information Content of Central Bank Paths
detail.abstract: Central banks publish projection paths, but these need not be optimal summaries of the information used to form them. We reframe conditional macroeconomic forecasting as an input problem: a fixed, pre-trained multivariate foundation time-series model reads the institution's historical predictions and announced future paths alongside target histories, rather than imposing the path as a model-consistent restriction inside a locally estimated system. The mapping nests the Mincer-Zarnowitz and Granger-Ramanathan regressions as its parametric-linear special case. Reading just Norges Bank's published path triple and target histories, the map cuts mean squared error against the Bank on inflation across horizons, and the nested combination regression puts the conditional weight on the map, not the path. A hard-conditioned VAR matched on the same future paths, but blind to the prediction record, is consistently outperformed on the rate and inflation, and the result survives the asymmetric-loss specifications that best rationalise the path. The VAR contrast replicates on Sweden and New Zealand; the institutional comparison only on New Zealand, with parity at best on Sweden. An institutional-learning regression rationalises the split: the Riksbank absorbs its recent misses more aggressively than Norges Bank and the RBNZ, leaving less residual signal to extract.

title: Traditional Cattle Fattening Practices in Karat-Zuria and Arba Minch-Zuria Woredas, South Ethiopia
affiliations: Southern Agricultural Research Institute (SARI) - Arba Minch Agricultural Research Center, Southern Agricultural Research Institute (SARI) - Arba Minch Agricultural Research Center, Southern Agricultural Research Institute (SARI) - Arba Minch Agricultural Research Center, affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Melbourne

detail.title: Traditional Cattle Fattening Practices in Karat-Zuria and Arba Minch-Zuria Woredas, South Ethiopia
detail.abstract: Smallholder cattle fattening is a key livelihood activity in south Ethiopia, providing income, meat, and draft power. This study assessed traditional cattle fattening practices, herd characteristics, feeding strategies, and market patterns in Karat-Zuria and Arba Minch-Zuria Woredas. A total of 104 households (66 from Karat-Zuria, 38 from Arba Minch-Zuria) were interviewed using structured questionnaires and field observations. Results showed that fattening practices were predominantly male-dominated (92.3%), with local cattle breeds preferred (63.5%). Farmers in Karat-Zuria preferred older cattle (>6 years), fed animals more frequently (5.64 ± 1.93 times/day), and fattened cattle for longer durations (5.3 ± 2.49 months) compared to Arba Minch-Zuria. Feeding was largely non-standardized, relying on local supplements. Seasonal fattening peaked during festivals (55.8%), and market destinations varied geographically. The findings highlight the need for improved feeding, age selection, and extension services to enhance productivity and profitability in smallholder fattening systems.

title: Minimum Wages and Race Disparities
affiliations: University of California, Irvine - Department of Economics and

detail.title: Minimum Wages and Race Disparities
detail.abstract: We provide a comprehensive analysis of the effects of minimum wages on blacks, and on the relative impacts on blacks vs. whites. We study not only teenagers – the focus of much of the minimum wage-employment literature – but also broader low-skill groups. We find no evidence that higher minimum wages reduce wage disparities. First, much of our evidence points to job loss effects from higher minimum wages are more evident for blacks – and more so for black men – but not detectable for whites. Second, in many of our analyses the effects of minimum wages are large enough to generate adverse effects on earnings (and relative earnings) of blacks. Third, given strong residential segregation by race in the United States, more adverse effects of minimum wages on blacks would fall on areas with a high black population share, and this appears to be accentuated by evidence that minimum wage effects are more adverse in areas where blacks are a very high share of the population, regardless of individual race.

title: Early Sorting Patterns in China's Inaugural Dual-Track Drug-List System: A Two-Stage Analysis of Manufacturer Submission and Final Listing Outcomes
affiliations: Wuhan University, Imperial College London, Tsinghua University, Wuhan University, Wuhan University and Wuhan University - Dong Fureng Institute of Economic and Social Development

detail.title: Early Sorting Patterns in China's Inaugural Dual-Track Drug-List System: A Two-Stage Analysis of Manufacturer Submission and Final Listing Outcomes

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: The study used only public administrative rosters and regulatory records, with no human participants or personal data, so ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: No specific grant from any funding agency.

detail.abstract:
Background: In 2025 China first ran two parallel pathways for medicines outside the basic list: medical-insurance negotiation and a commercial-insurance innovative-drug list. Earlier analyses conflated manufacturer submission with final listing.

Methods: We censused all 353 products passing 2025 formal review (330 Western; 324 with cost data) and modelled commercial-track submission (stage 1) and final inclusion within each applicant pool (stage 2: medical pool 282/106 events; commercial pool 115/18), using Firth penalised-likelihood regression with profile-likelihood intervals; band-dummy models were primary, ordinal models sensitivity analyses.

Findings: 114 products entered medical insurance and 19 the commercial list. Commercial submission was price-graded (over-500k RMB aOR 21.0, 95% PL CI 6.3-108.5) and more frequent for rare-disease products (aOR 2.79, 1.27-6.19); first-in-class status was imprecise after adjustment (aOR 2.28, p=0.10). Medical-pool inclusion varied non-monotonically with cost, peaking in the RMB 50,000-200,000 band (aOR 10.4, 4.8-24.9), and less likely with more prior applications (aOR 0.41, 0.26-0.60). Commercial-pool inclusion was concentrated at the high-price end: 0 of 49 applicants below 50,000 RMB/year were included versus 18 of 66 at or above (FIC aOR 0.59, 0.16-1.95; ordinal price slope aOR 3.67, 2.10-7.81). The formal relay pathway’s safety-net role cannot be determined from end-of-cycle outcomes.

Interpretation: Price is associated with both commercial-track submission and inclusion; novelty shows a crude association with submission only. The inaugural commercial list is a price-sorted upper tier from a self-selected expensive pool; listing is not enrolment, reimbursement or access.

title: Queensland's COVID-19 Surveillance: A Bayesian Markov Chain Monte Carlo Analysis
affiliations: Central Queensland Hospital and Health Service - Central Queensland Public Health Unit, Australian Government - Communicable Diseases and Surveillance Section, Charles Darwin University - Global and Tropical Health Division, Children’s Hospital at Westmead - The National Centre for Immunisation Research and Surveillance (NCIRS) and Central Queensland Hospital and Health Service - Central Queensland Public Health Unit

detail.title: Queensland's COVID-19 Surveillance: A Bayesian Markov Chain Monte Carlo Analysis

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: An exemption from full ethics review was granted by the Metro North Ethics Committee (EX/2026/MNH/128449).
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this study. This research was conducted as part of routine public health activities of Queensland Health.

detail.abstract:
Background: Queensland maintained COVID-19 elimination until 13 December 2021, entering the Omicron era as a population immunologically naïve to natural infection. Progressive disengagement from PCR-based surveillance created a progressive, time-varying gap between true infections and notified cases throughout 2022.

Methods: Anchored to four rounds of anti-nucleocapsid seroprevalence data, a Bayesian Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) model implemented in Stan estimated quarterly true incident infections across 2022. Case data from the Queensland Notifiable Conditions System were classified into three detection pathways. Quarterly under-ascertainment factors (UAFs), corrected case-hospitalisation rates (cCHR), and corrected infected case fatality rates (cCFR) were derived as generated quantities with full posterior uncertainty propagation.

Results: From 1,433,946 notified cases, the model estimated 4,266,932 true incident infections (95% CrI 3,980,094–4,711,125; cumulative population attack rate 80.8%) in 2022. The cumulative UAF was 2.98 (2.78–3.29), rising from 2.35 (2.08–2.68) in Q1 to 4.08 (2.41–6.38) in Q4. The cCHR rose from 0.457% (0.397%–0.525%) in Q1 and 0.401% (0.330%–0.493%) in Q2, to 1.351% (0.868%–2.318%) in Q4. For 2022, the annual crude case fatality was 0.16%, whilst cCFR was much lower at 0.055% (0.049%–0.059%).

Conclusion: Based on our MCMC analysis, fewer than one in three SARS-CoV-2 infections were formally notified in Queensland during 2022. The quarterly UAF estimates and corrected severity metrics provide validated inputs for modified burden-of-disease estimation and vaccine effectiveness studies. This framework is generalisable to future ascertainment work for notifiable and emerging pathogens.

title: Do Investors Herd in Green Hydrogen Stocks? Market States, Liquidity, and Energy-Supply Shocks
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Africa Business School, Université de Pau et des Pays de l'Adour and Excelia Business School

detail.title: Do Investors Herd in Green Hydrogen Stocks? Market States, Liquidity, and Energy-Supply Shocks
detail.abstract: The financial behaviour of hydrogen equities has so far been examined at the level of broad thematic or cross-asset indices. Those are dominated by diversified industrials of which the green hydrogen value chain represents a minority or even negligible share of activities. We take the equal-weighted return of seventeen pure-play constituents of the Solactive Global Hydrogen index (SOLGHYD) as the market return, isolating them with a transparent purity screen that removes eight diversified names. Herding is tested with the cross-sectional absolute deviation framework of Chang et al. (2000) on daily data from January 2018 to June 2026. Aggregate stability masks a strongly state-dependent behaviour: convergence emerges in falling markets, under medium and, more weakly, high liquidity, and during the Russia-Ukraine war (weakly during the Covid-19 outbreak), a pattern consistent with loss-averse, fear-driven mimicry when the shared transition narrative deteriorates. During the 2026 closure of the Strait of Hormuz the segment instead anti-herds, dispersion widening more than proportionately as the energy-supply shock separates constituents by their fossil-price exposure. These dynamics bear on the pricing and cost of capital of a listed segment central to the energy transition.

title: Are Fractional Share Trades Informative?
affiliations: University of Mississippi, University of Mississippi and University of Notre Dame - Department of Finance

detail.title: Are Fractional Share Trades Informative?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I have nothing to declare.
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract: Recent literature suggests coordinated fractional share trading impacts stock prices. We provide evidence that at least one retail broker systematically executes fractional share orders in batches on a daily basis between 2023 and 2024. For example, during a 5000-millisecond time interval on March 7, 2024, over 65,000 inferred fractional share trades execute in Tesla. We construct a methodology to systematically identify these ‘bursts’ of inferred fractional share trades and use them to investigate whether the batched execution of fractional share orders has price impact. Despite the fact that over 93% of the inferred fractional share trades in bursts are buyer-initiated, both univariate and multivariate analyses indicate that bursts of inferred fractional share trades do not impact underlying security prices.

title: John Nash's Bargaining Parabola
affiliations: Criterion Economics, LLC

detail.title: John Nash's Bargaining Parabola

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that neither he nor Criterion Economics, Inc. has been retained as an expert, consultant, or witness in any of the cases discussed in this article. The author has no personal or financial relationship with any person or organization that could be perceived to have influenced this article.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The author is solely responsible for its content.

detail.abstract:
When a damages expert derives a reasonable royalty as a remedy for patent infringement from Nobel laureate John Nash’s bargaining solution, the expert reports a division of surplus that the parties’ conduct never produced. The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit rejected that methodology in VirnetX v. Cisco on a narrow ground: the Nash bargaining solution says nothing about which real-world disputes satisfy its premises. Left unexamined in VirnetX was the equal weighting built into Nash’s multiplication.


The Nash bargaining solution maximizes the multiplicative product of the parties’ gains above their disagreement payoffs. In the symmetric case, the objective function is a parabola and the even split sits at its vertex. But that symmetry is not a fact about the parties. It is an axiom of Nash’s mathematical model. Because each party’s utility scale is separately calibrated, one party’s utility unit cannot be treated as commensurable with the other’s. Multiplying the two therefore builds equal weighting into the model arbitrarily and reports the resulting split of surplus as though it had been measured from the parties’ bargaining power, rather than assumed by construction.

 

Reasonable-royalty litigation requires a case-specific estimate of the license that the parties would have struck in a hypothetical negotiation. An expert economic witness on patent-infringement damages who begins with the Nash multiplicative product instead supplies the vertex of a function that fixes symmetry before any inquiry into the case-specific evidence—such as bargaining power, outside options, and patience—that the Georgia-Pacific factors are designed to elicit. In Daubert terms, the expert has not supplied a basis for the division of surplus; he has supplied an assumption disguised as a conclusion. That method does not multiply; it measures.

 

Federal Rule of Evidence 702, as amended in 2023, and the Federal Circuit’s en banc decision in EcoFactor, Inc. v. Google LLC in 2025 require the proponent of expert testimony to establish the sufficiency of the basis for an opinion, not merely its relevance. For the equal division of surplus at the heart of Nash’s bargaining parabola, no such basis exists, because the 50-percent split was never measured from facts concerning the parties, their patience, or their alternatives. The split of surplus was merely assumed by the choice of a symmetric, multiplicative objective function—the same choice that recurs, under other names, in disputes over fair, reasonable, and nondiscriminatory (FRAND) royalties for standard-essential patents (SEPs).

detail.abstract: Textbook insurance pricing ties a property's premium to its own hazard exposure: riskier properties pay higher premiums. But institutional investors in commercial real estate do not buy coverage one property at a time; they negotiate it for their entire fund portfolio. We examine whether, and by how much, the disaster-risk profile of the portfolio is capitalized into the insurance cost recorded against individual properties. Matching property-level insurance expense from the National Council of Real Estate Investment Fiduciaries (NCREIF) to modeled expected disaster damage from Moody's Risk Management Solutions (RMS), we find that a property's insurance cost depends on the fund portfolio it sits in. Holding own hazard exposure fixed, insurance expense rises with the mean risk of the fund portfolio and falls with the fund's scale and risk diversification. A transaction-based design that tracks the same property as it moves between funds with different risk profiles confirms the pattern. The two designs agree on the magnitude: a 10 percent increase in the average disaster risk of the surrounding portfolio raises a property's insurance cost by roughly 0.4 percent. Because insurance expense is charged directly against net operating income (NOI), portfolio-level pricing implies that otherwise identical assets can differ in their NOIs and thus underwriting values according to the portfolios that hold them, with implications for disaster-risk measurement, disclosure, and the allocation of climate-exposed assets across institutional owners.

detail.abstract: This working paper examines, in prospective terms and from the standpoint of the political economy of security, how the reactivation of the Venezuelan oil industry along the border strip with Colombia coexists with an armed economy of extortion, hiring control, and collection of protection payments ("vacunas") that the National Liberation Army (ELN), FARC dissident factions, and the Bolivarian Liberation Front (FBL/FPLN), the latter of Venezuelan origin, have sustained in that same corridor for more than four decades. The analysis deliberately moves from the state level down to the municipal level: it examines by name the Guafita and La Victoria oil fields and the towns of Guasdualito, El Amparo, and Elorza, in Apure state, documenting well counts, basin geography, and patterns of fuel and strategic material smuggling, together with the available evidence of complicity by civilian and military officials. The paper describes, step by step, the mechanism through which these structures condition the operations of PDVSA and its contractors on the hiring of affiliated personnel, documents their record of kidnappings and killings of oil engineers and workers along the Arauca-Apure-Táchira-Zulia axis, and presents evidence that the ELN has established, in the very municipality of Elorza, Apure state, a training school for armed drone pilots whose graduates have already been deployed against Colombian oil infrastructure in Arauca and the Catatumbo, which turns the protection of Venezuelan oil facilities against this threat into a prospective priority. As an applied contribution, it proposes the Sanabria Protocol for Protection of the Border Oil Supply Chain, which starts from an explicit principle of no negotiation with armed structures and of license disqualification for any operator that negotiates with or conceals that scheme, together with payroll verification, financial intelligence, protected reporting, institutional vetting of the chain of command, and binational cooperation with the United States, subject at every stage to judicial control, proportionality, and human rights safeguards. The model is presented as a public policy hypothesis subject to empirical validation, not as a determination of causality between insecurity and investment.

detail.abstract: This research note examines onion purchasing behaviour and consumer perceptions of market performance in Bangladesh. A structured online questionnaire was administered from 15 to 19 July 2026 through personal contacts, university networks, and social-media and messaging channels. Of 66 consenting respondents, 46 had purchased onion for household consumption during the previous 30 days and met the purchase eligibility criterion. All participants were independently verified as adults. The non-probability sample was predominantly young and urban, and all eligible respondents reported bachelor-level education or above. Analysis used frequencies, percentages, medians, interquartile ranges, and item-level top-two response shares. Nearby availability attracted 84.8% agreement, but only 30.4% agreed that good-quality onion was affordable to low-income consumers; 50.0% believed onion remained obtainable without long delays during shortages. Although 76.1% regarded the survey-period price as reasonable, 60.9% reported that they would buy a smaller quantity after a sharp price increase. Respondents associated prices with transport costs (73.9%), intermediaries (71.7%), and storage costs (65.2%). Better supply-chain management attracted 82.6% agreement, while 54.3% expressed no or low trust in government price monitoring. These findings distinguish routine physical availability from perceived affordability and shortage resilience. They offer exploratory evidence from a small convenience sample and do not estimate national market performance, demand elasticity, or causal policy effects.

title: Free Speech Protection and Local Government Stewardship: Evidence from State Anti-SLAPP Laws

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None of the authors have known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: Ke Wang acknowledges the Insight Development Grants from the Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council of Canada (Project No. 430-2026-01794). Liandong Zhang acknowledges financial support from the Lee Kong Chian Professorship.

detail.abstract: We examine whether and how free speech protection affects local government stewardship. Using staggered enactments of state anti-SLAPP statutes, which limit strategic lawsuits against public participation (SLAPPs), we find economically meaningful improvements in local government stewardship following enactments, as reflected in timelier financial reporting and fewer material fiscal concerns. These effects are stronger for states with more potent anti-SLAPP laws and for governments with a mayor–council structure, but weaker for governments with greater congressional representation and stricter state-level fiscal monitoring. In addition, we find increases in civic engagement and local media coverage of government-related issues, along with less favorable reelection outcomes for incumbents after anti-SLAPP enactments. Convicted corruption also declines, consistent with free speech protection curbing public officials’ resource diversion. Finally, municipal bond trading spreads narrow following the enactments of anti-SLAPP laws, suggesting that investors price the resulting improvements in stewardship. Overall, our results show that strengthening free speech protection improves public-sector stewardship by facilitating public scrutiny and sustaining accountability.

detail.abstract: Emotional intelligence constitutes a key component of human capital, shaped partially by educational materials. Using machine learning and generative AI tools, we examine emotional content in public-school textbooks and children's literature. A stark mismatch emerges: text exposes children to a broad emotional range, but images overwhelmingly depict happiness and calm, regardless of emotions described in text on the same page. Nearly half of pages show zero overlap between the emotions described in text and those shown in images. This pattern persists across time, contexts, and identities. Household purchases and library inventories suggest content may be endogenously shaped by consumer demand favoring "positive" cover imagery, implying market forces narrow the emotional landscape children encounter.

title: Beyond Geographic Proximity: The Role of Attribute Similarity in Multiscale Local Regression Models

detail.title: Beyond Geographic Proximity: The Role of Attribute Similarity in Multiscale Local Regression Models

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflict of interest.

detail.abstract: Recent studies have increasingly incorporated attribute information into the spatial weighting schemes of local regression models in both single-scale and multiscale frameworks. However, limited attention has been given to when attribute information is necessary, how it should be interpreted, and how it shapes coefficient surfaces. To address this, two simulations are conducted: one examines the effects of geographic and attribute-based weights on coefficient surfaces, and the other evaluates performance under varying levels of predictor collinearity. Additionally, a statistical test is proposed to assess whether the improvement in model performance attributable to attribute similarity is statistically significant. To conduct our analyses, multiscale geographically weighted regression (MGWR) and multiscale similarity-based geographically weighted regression (M-SGWR) models are adopted. While MGWR defines spatial interaction solely through geographic proximity, M-SGWR allows interaction to be governed jointly by geographic proximity and attribute similarity among locations. The findings indicate that when the underlying coefficient surface is genuinely smooth and relatively simple, geographical proximity alone is sufficient to uncover spatial heterogeneity in the relationships between variables across space; however, insufficient for complex and non-smooth spatial heterogeneity. Thus, incorporating attribute information into the model substantially improves the model's ability to recover the true spatial processes. Furthermore, under high collinearity between predictors, incorporating attribute information can help mitigate multicollinearity by defining neighborhoods in both geographical and attribute spaces. Broadly, these findings suggest that some spatial processes cannot be explained solely by the physical proximity of locations, as the underlying relationships may be multidimensional and more complex.

title:
AI Knowledge Architecture 
Why Organizations Do Not Yet Own the Knowledge Their AI Systems Produce
affiliations: Independent

detail.title:
AI Knowledge Architecture 
Why Organizations Do Not Yet Own the Knowledge Their AI Systems Produce

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests that could have influenced the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This conceptual architecture study did not involve human participants, personal data, or empirical research requiring ethics approval.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Organizations increasingly rely on large language models to interpret their own documents: requirements, policies, contracts, specifications, and operational records. Retrieval-augmented generation, knowledge graphs, and memory systems have made the underlying material far easier to reach. But reaching information is not the same as keeping what was concluded about it. When an AI system determines what a requirement means, which conditions it applies under, and how it relates to another commitment, that determination typically exists only inside the response it produced. The next interaction begins from the source text again. The information persists. The interpretation does not. This paper argues that the consequence is organizational rather than merely technical. If an accepted interpretation is never represented as anything other than a past model output, the organization cannot say which interpretations it has committed to, cannot distinguish an established position from a newly generated one, and cannot demonstrate afterwards why a particular reading was adopted. Interpretive work is performed repeatedly, paid for repeatedly, and owned by no one. AI Knowledge Architecture addresses this by applying a governing principle: once an interpretation has been explicitly established and accepted, it should not be re-inferred. The architecture places an explicit admission boundary between interpretations an AI system proposes and interpretations an organization has accepted, and it externalizes accepted interpretations into persistent, inspectable structures-a stable identity for each knowledge assertion, explicit representation of the semantics that were resolved, the relationships that were accepted, the conditions under which those relationships hold, the basis on which they were accepted, and the recurring perspectives through which the same knowledge is organized for different roles. The architecture does not attempt to make probabilistic AI deterministic, and it does not replace retrieval, knowledge graphs, provenance models, or ontology views. Retrieval locates material; AI reasoning proposes interpretations; admission determines which of them become governed knowledge; persistent structure allows later work to use accepted meaning without rebuilding it. An illustrative case-a single performance requirement read by architecture, business, product, and operations roles-shows how one shared knowledge state can support genuinely different interpretive organizations without fragmenting into separate stores, and how a cost-versus-capacity conflict becomes visible only when those organizations are compared.

title: The Operational Resilience Paradox: Socio-Technical Decoupling and Failover Invariance in Systemic Infrastructure: A Formal Empirical Evaluation

detail.title: The Operational Resilience Paradox: Socio-Technical Decoupling and Failover Invariance in Systemic Infrastructure: A Formal Empirical Evaluation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests that could have influenced the work reported in this prospectus.

detail.abstract: Supervisory oversight frameworks for systemic financial infrastructure-notably Canada's Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) Guideline E-21 on Operational Risk and Resilience (published August 2024; industry adherence expected September 2026), the European Union's Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA, Regulation EU 2022/2554, Articles 11 & 24), and the Monetary Authority of Singapore's (MAS) Technology Risk Management (TRM) Guidelines (published January 18, 2021)-mandate deterministic proofs of operational recoverability. In response, global financial institutions have heavily deployed software-defined multi-region redundancy, public cloud containerized orchestrations on hyperscale infrastructure (specifically Azure Kubernetes Service / AKS), and active-active failover topologies. Despite these investments, catastrophic failovers persist during unscripted operational shocks. This paper provides an empirical and mathematical treatment of the Operational Resilience Paradox: technical failovers fail not due to binary hardware flaws, but due to Socio-Technical Decoupling between organizational governance structures and automated infrastructure layers. Integrating Socio-Technical Systems (STS) Theory with high-availability distributed systems principles, this study models the non-linear boundaries of Recovery Time Achieved (RT A) versus Recovery Time Objective (RT O). The framework evaluates empirical, anonymized enterprise operational paradigms: (1) First-Line Control Testing Methodologies; (2) Global IT Disaster Recovery Standard Operating Procedures; (3) Crossborder Asia-Pacific production topologies; and (4) Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) schema decoupling across risk registers, architecture configuration platforms, and continuity management engines. We model human-in-the-loop decision stalls (∆t decision), formalize the conditions under which manual attestations mask latent failure, examine high-profile industry collapses, and define an empirically validated Four-Pillar Deterministic Resilience Architecture.

title: Concept Programming for Dependable AI

detail.title: Concept Programming for Dependable AI

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.ethicsApproval: None

detail.abstract: A language-grounded neural system arrives with an endowment. The literature and other material used to train it lay down the distinctions it can already draw. Every concept an engineer wants to instill therefore meets that endowment as its initial condition, and different concepts meet different conditions. This paper introduces Concept Programming, a method that measures those initial conditions, supplies what the substrate lacks, trains the concept as a named positive attractor, and verifies the result against a requirement stated in advance. Four experiments on two open model families test the method on a consumer laptop. Experiment 1 raises adherence to governance constraints from 47.2 percent to 94.4 percent (95 percent CI 81.9 to 98.5; Fisher exact p < 0.0001), with transfer to domains absent from training. Experiment 2 extends the method from constraints to value systems. Experiment 3 charts the learning curve and shows that 200 cases do not reach certification grade under prompt-level injection. Experiment 4 removes the judge model, moves to a second model family, and instills three concepts under low-rank adaptation against a specification of 0.02 maximum miss rate. A probe measured each concept's constituent distinctions on the base model before training. One concept lacked two of three constituents; training supplied them first, and the concept then met its specification in a single round. Across three concepts and more than twenty rounds, every trained frame family reached exactly zero misses, and every residual error fell in a frame family withheld from training. Performance therefore forms two populations rather than one rate. On covered forms, zero misses in 400 to 480 cases place the true miss rate below 0.02 with confidence above 0.999 for all three concepts. A deployment meets the specification whenever violations arriving in uncovered forms hold below a computable share of traffic, which measures 0.800, 0.235, and 0.047 for the three concepts. The method locates its own exceptions and names the form each one occupies. 1. Concept Programming, a method that trains a behavioral constraint as a named positive attractor paired with an explicit response, drawing training instances from the concept's semantic case frame.

title: Role Separation Beats Process Structure: An Experimental Comparison of AI-assisted Startup Ideation Methods

detail.title: Role Separation Beats Process Structure: An Experimental Comparison of AI-assisted Startup Ideation Methods

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests. For transparency: the author designed and taught the university course in which the experimental workshop was embedded, and also served as one of the three rating instances (as blinded instructor, with ideas rated under randomized codes). This dual role and the associated limitations are disclosed and discussed in the paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: The study was embedded in a regular university course activity. No personal data were collected: startup ideas were elicited and rated under randomized codes (A–L), team profiles were gathered anonymously through a non-personal two-stage questionnaire, and peer ratings are stored only as per-idea aggregate means. Given the fully anonymous, non-sensitive nature of the data, no formal ethics committee approval was obtained; the anonymization and consent procedure is documented in the study's reproducibility package (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22286918).

detail.abstract:
Generative AI is now used routinely for startup ideation. How exactly the interaction between founding teams and large language models (LLMs) should be structured, by contrast, has hardly been studied. We report the conduct and results of a controlled quasi-experiment comparing four ideation conditions in a time-boxed university innovation workshop (N = 16 participants, four teams, 12 startup ideas): human-only ideation (control group), unstructured AI use, a structured Expand-Critique-Converge prompting framework (ECC), and that same framework with the AI's functions separated into three distinct roles (Ideator, Critic, and Synthesizer), executed in separate chat sessions (ECC-R). Idea quality was then assessed on three dimensions (problem-solution fit, market potential, feasibility) by three independent instances: a blinded instructor, cross-team peers, and model-controlled post-hoc ratings by a generative AI.
Contrary to expectations, the standard ECC condition performed worst across all rating instances, while ECC with role separation produced the highest-rated ideas (mean d = +2.88 vs. standard ECC on the total score), placing all three of its ideas in the overall top five. Process structure alone did not improve idea quality; separating the AI's generative and evaluative roles did. Two methodological findings qualify the evaluation itself. First, AI ratings produced within the generation session exceeded external post-hoc ratings of the same ideas by 1.67 points on a 15-point scale (d = 1.38), indicating a self-enhancement bias concentrated on the problem–solution-fit and market dimensions. Second, inter-rater agreement across instructor, peers, and AI was poor (Krippendorff's α < 0.11 on all dimensions), whereas agreement between two independent AI models was high (ICC = 0.85, r_s = 0.82). We discuss implications for prompt-and-process design in AI-assisted ideation, for AI-assisted assessment in entrepreneurship education, and for the emerging LLM-as-a-judge literature, and we document how the findings were fed back into an evidence-based framework iteration (ECC v4.0).

detail.abstract: This paper examines Vinted, a peer-to-peer resale marketplace, as a case study in circular business-model growth. In 2025, Vinted reported revenue of €1.1 billion, a 38% increase year on year, driven entirely by the recirculation of existing goods rather than new production. Positioning Vinted against Shein (a linear fast-fashion model) and ThredUp (a curated resale model), the paper argues that circularity does not inherently constrain growth; the binding constraint is a venture's capacity to reduce transactional friction. It then engages the rebound-effect objection, using Vinted's own reported 76% substitution rate to assess whether resale genuinely displaces new consumption or simply expands total consumption. The paper concludes that Vinted's environmental benefit is best explained not by shifting consumer values toward sustainability, but by aligning the economically rational choice with the environmentally preferable one, a mechanism with broader implications for responsible entrepreneurship research.

title: From Generation to Specification: Fast Natural Language Sports Q&A Across LLMs

detail.title: From Generation to Specification: Fast Natural Language Sports Q&A Across LLMs

detail.abstract:
A coach or broadcast analyst following a live match may have only a few seconds between
points to get an answer. A pre-built dashboard cannot anticipate every question, but a natural-
language system can, provided it produces a reliable answer quickly enough to be useful while
the match is still unfolding. This paper asks whether a large language model can accurately
answer an unanticipated question about a live sports match within that brief window.

The conventional approach is to have the LLM write SQL and hope the query is correct.
In this study, the model instead specifies what it wants to calculate using a small, fixed set
of pre-built building blocks that we call QueryIR, or Query Intermediate Representation. The
model describes the analysis, and a deterministic engine that was built and tested in advance
executes the computation directly. This shifts the burden of implementation from the language
model to the engine.

The evaluation uses one frozen, synthetically derived tennis match, a held-out set of two
hundred questions written after the system was frozen, and six language models spanning both
proprietary and open-weight systems. A smaller robustness check repeats the same two paths
on one real match logged by the Match Charting Project on Tennis Abstract, a volunteer
project in which people chart matches point by point. The main contribution is the head-to-
head comparison: the same questions, SQL versus QueryIR, with accuracy and end-to-end time
reported together. The models that struggled to write SQL gained accuracy without becoming
faster: Qwen about 60% more correct answers at almost the same clock. The models that
already wrote strong SQL finished in about half the time. Haiku gained about 50% more
correct answers and was slightly faster. When asked to tally the event log directly from prose,
the models scored only four percent on the simplest count class, whereas SQL and QueryIR
both achieved one hundred percent on those same questions.

The results do not establish that this pattern generalizes beyond the two evaluations reported
here. Within the evaluation, however, three of the six models completed the QueryIR path in
just a few seconds per question, putting the response time within a range that could be relevant
during a live match. The paper concludes that moving the boundary between the model and the
execution engine can improve both accuracy and speed, though the direction of the improvement
depends on the model.

title: AI-Augmented Green Jobs and Corporate Climate Performance: Evidence from U.S. Firms and Facilities

detail.title: AI-Augmented Green Jobs and Corporate Climate Performance: Evidence from U.S. Firms and Facilities

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No
declarations.funderStatement: No

detail.abstract: Whether green job positions (GJPs) improve corporate environmental performance remains theoretically contested. The resource-based view (RBV) predicts that GJPs build the environmental capabilities firms need to substantively address climate problems, whereas institutional theory suggests that firms may adopt such positions primarily for compliance and reputation purposes. We reconcile these conflicting predictions by considering how GJPs are equipped with artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities. We theorize that AI skills serve as complementary resources that convert green domain expertise into substantive environmental action, and that their cost and scarcity leave purely symbolic adopters little incentive to acquire them. Using panel data from 587 U.S. public firms and 1,500 facilities between 2010 and 2022, we find that GJPs augmented with AI skills are associated with significant emission reductions. In contrast, GJPs without AI skills do not create such environmental benefits. The effect of GJPs augmented by AI is more pronounced in regions with high climate-change-related opportunities and when AIenhanced GJPs are situated at the mid-level of the organizational hierarchy, where operational decisions are implemented. To uncover the underlying mechanism, we examine firms' green patents, especially those incorporating AI technologies. We find that firms with AI-augmented GJPs generate more AI-related green patents, indicating that AI equips green employees to translate domain expertise into substantive technological and process innovations rather than symbolic compliance. Overall, our findings identify AI as a complementary digital capability that determines whether green human capital delivers the substantive environmental improvements predicted by the RBV or remains limited to the symbolic role anticipated by institutional theory.

detail.abstract: In the modern digital economy, critical infrastructure across the finance, healthcare, government, and energy sectors is increasingly dependent on software systems built by human developers operating within complex and restrictive regulatory environments. While regulatory oversight is essential for maintaining security, transparency, and public trust, the associated compliance burden introduces significant friction into the software development lifecycle. This friction has measurable downstream consequences, including reduced velocity, increased error rates, psychological burnout, and systemic operational risk. Despite the strategic importance of these environments, current academic and industry models do not provide an objective, standardized method to measure how regulatory constraints and enterprise tooling architectures impact the lived experience of developers or how this experience translates into measurable business and security outcomes. This study introduces the Developer Experience Measurement Framework (DX-MF), a quantitative, multi-dimensional model designed to measure, analyze, and optimize developer experience in regulated enterprises. The framework comprises five novel indices: The Onboarding Friction Index (OFI), Workflow Interruption Rate (WIR), Compliance Interaction Load (CIL), Toolchain Efficiency Score (TES), and Cognitive Load Index (CLI). A sixteen-week empirical case study conducted in a major financial institution demonstrates that strategic interventions such as Policy-as-Code implementation, developer platform standardization, and compliance automation led to a 65% improvement in overall Developer Experience, a 47% increase in delivery velocity, a 60% reduction in support burden, and a significant decline in reported cognitive strain. This study contributes a new operational lens through which regulated enterprises can evaluate systemic risk, productivity potential, and modernization priorities. Furthermore, it establishes the study of Regulated Developer Experience Engineering as an emerging discipline at the intersection of software engineering, organizational psychology, compliance science, and national infrastructure resilience.

detail.abstract: Regulatory barriers and capital inefficiencies represent persistent vulnerabilities in corporate global supply chains. Within the framework of United States import structures, Foreign Trade Zones (FTZs) provide vehicles for optimization, primarily through duty deferral, automated classification shielding via Privileged Foreign status, and systemic reduction of transaction costs. This paper presents an eventdriven architectural blueprint that translates physical distribution and warehouse operational occurrences directly into valid customs declarations. We examine the transaction stream mapping required to dynamically execute CBP Forms 214, 7512, and 7501. By evaluating the integration of Harbor Maintenance Fees (HMF) and the systemic consolidation of Merchandise Processing Fees (MPF) via Oracle GTM Release 26A, this study proves that modern automated trade systems can successfully isolate companies from tariff volatility, streamline cash requirements, and guarantee legal compliance under rigorous statutory audit standards.

title:

detail.title:

Deterministic Safety Evaluation of Intent-based AI Agents for Enterprise Private Networks

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA
declarations.ethicsApproval: NA

detail.abstract: Enterprise private 5G/LTE and emerging private 6G systems increasingly support safety-critical applications in hospitals, factories, warehouses, ports, energy sites, data centers, and campuses. Intent-based AI agents can translate operator goals into network actions, but private-network control requires explicit preservation of security, privacy, data locality, critical-service priority, human approval, rollback, and auditability. This paper introduces AgentPN Benchmark Test, a deterministic decision-safety benchmark for evaluating intent-based AI agents before they interact with enterprise private-network control surfaces. AgentPN contains 210 synthetic expertdesigned scenarios organized across seven enterprise verticals and six horizontal task families. Each public case exposes site context, network state, operator intent, policies, evidence, architecture metadata, and neutral candidate actions; hidden ground truth specifies required, optional, approval-gated, and forbidden actions together with locality, validation, rollback, audit, risk, and criticality requirements. Agent outputs are restricted to a structured JSON schema and are scored by deterministic script-based PASS/PARTIAL/UNSAFE/INVALID rules rather than LLM-asjudge evaluation. A 420-run evaluation of two OpenRouter-routed open-weight model endpoints shows that gpt-oss-120b attains 44.8% PASS, 20.0% PARTIAL, 9.5% UNSAFE, and 25.7% INVALID outcomes, while gpt-oss-20b attains 24.3% PASS and 32.9% UNSAFE outcomes. We further quantify operational exposure using resource-, cost-, and timeline-impact equations, showing how unsafe-agent rates amplify in high-velocity automation settings. AgentPN is a readiness filter: an agent that fails it should not be considered ready for private-network control under the benchmarked enterprise constraints.

title: Emergent Dynamics in Complex Systems: A Diagnostic Framework for Regime, Singularity, and Chaos Identification in Nonlinear Systems

detail.abstract:
This paper develops a unified nonlinear-dynamics diagnostic framework for identifying emergent patterns, regime structures, and transition dynamics across causal systems of almost any type and scale, spanning the natural and social sciences. Rather than estimating specific models or analysing particular datasets, the paper establishes the theoretical and methodological logic required to infer underlying dynamic regimes from observable system behaviour. Innovation and knowledge systems are used as an illustrative application, but the framework is explicitly general and domain-independent. 

The analysis addresses a central limitation of conventional empirical and theoretical approaches, which typically impose linear, equilibrium-centred, or steady-state assumptions that are ill-suited to systems characterised by feedback, path dependence, nonlinearity, and structural transformation. Building on canonical results from nonlinear dynamics (e.g. Strogatz) and related complexity traditions, the paper constructs a typology of emergent regimes, including fixed points, bifurcations, limit cycles, multistability, singularity, synchronization, and chaos, and maps each regime to its characteristic diagnostic signatures in observable data. 

For each class of dynamics, the work formally specifies the associated temporal, cross sectional, and spatiotemporal patterns, stability properties, and local indicators required for empirical identification, without presupposing a particular functional form, dataset, or disciplinary context. This yields a general-purpose inference architecture capable of detecting latent dynamic structure across heterogeneous systems. 

The framework further clarifies how exogenous or endogenous shocks, such as advances in artificial intelligence, might alter system dynamics by modifying feedback strength, coordination structures, and the effective dimensionality of state spaces, thereby inducing transitions across regimes. 

The paper contributes a domain-general methodological foundation for emergent pattern diagnostics, bridging nonlinear dynamics, complexity science, and causal inference, and providing a scalable toolkit for analysing dynamic systems ranging from biological and physical processes to economic, technological, and social systems.

detail.abstract: In 2025, Grindr's chief executive noted the New York Stock Exchange-listed company's forthcoming artificial intelligence would learn from the private messages of its users rather than their profiles, on grounds that conversations reveal a more authentic version of users than selfauthored disclosure. This paper looks at the resultant shift from a disclosure-based architecture, through which users present themselves to one another, to one based on inference, in which a platform's own conclusions about users are returned to them as findings. Drawing on theoretical frameworks of autonomy and performative risk, this paper asserts that the turn to user inference details an underlying harm to user autonomy. By substituting algorithmic accuracy for genuine authenticity, the platform's own intelligence layer reduces the agency of its users while creating non-auditable mechanism of predictive sorting. Ultimately, the paper concludes that a necessary corrective to this algorithmic extraction is structural contestability rather than technical accuracy.

title: Seeing the Other Half of Medicaid: A Generative AI Measurement Infrastructure for Open Government Claims Data
affiliations: University of California, San Diego (UCSD) - Rady School of Management

detail.title: Seeing the Other Half of Medicaid: A Generative AI Measurement Infrastructure for Open Government Claims Data

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author reports no financial or personal interests that could have influenced the research reported in this work.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was supported by the National Science Foundation (NSF) under grant number 2427505.

detail.abstract: Governments increasingly release large administrative datasets, but these data cannot support research until operational codes are translated into meaningful constructs. We study this problem in the 2026 U.S. government release of provider-level Medicaid spending, which contains 238 million records and $994.7 billion in provider-attributable payments from 2018 to 2024. The standard available taxonomy leaves nearly half of these dollars unclassified. The missing territory includes major Medicaid services such as personal care, community behavioral health, and home-and community-based long-term services. Available labeled data come largely from Medicare-covered codes and exclude many of the Medicaid-specific categories that dominate this gap, which limits supervised classifiers trained on those labels. We develop CLAIM (Classification via LLM with Auditable Iterative Mapping), a generative AI measurement infrastructure that uses a large language model (LLM) to bring institutional knowledge into the measurement process while keeping its judgments auditable. CLAIM combines a purpose-built and versioned Medicaid Service Taxonomy, explicit abstention when a code's meaning is uncertain, complete provenance logs, and a prespecified human-expert audit with versioned correction. We classify the 3,200 highest-spend codes, covering 99.81% of analysis-set dollars. The audit confirmed 94.6% of substantively classified sampled codes, representing 98.7% of sampled dollars, and audit-based extrapolation estimates residual misclassification at 0.29% of dollars, with 2.5% under a conservative sensitivity calculation. A known-shock validation shows the measured categories reproduce the expected pattern of utilization disruption during the April 2020 COVID-19 lockdown. The measurement layer enables a national service-level census of provider-attributable Medicaid spending, event-study evidence on service-specific utilization changes around the Medicaid unwinding, and a transparent provider-integrity screen. More broadly, the study shows how generative AI can serve as a governed research instrument when administrative data are public but the measurement infrastructure needed to study them is incomplete.

detail.abstract: AI agents are increasingly being considered for private 5G/6G network management, including slice changes, device authorization, workload placement, emergency response, and audit-oriented operation. Static or one-shot evaluation misses trust failures that appear only when state persists and earlier actions influence later observations. This paper introduces AgentPN Loop, a deterministic, stateful benchmark for closedloop enterprise private-network management. AgentPN Loop is a management-plane benchmark, not a packet-level wireless simulator. It contains 100 episodes, 10 steps per episode, 1,000 decision points, and seven enterprise verticals. The dataset uses a hybrid real/synthetic construction: public datasets anchor external operational pressure, while deterministic synthetic rules generate private-network state, policies, approvals, rollback checkpoints, expected actions, unsafe actions, and scoring labels. AgentPN Loop supports canonical evaluation, where every agent receives the same fixed trajectory, and interactive evaluation, where the model's own prior actions become part of later state and history. We evaluate GPT-OSS-20B run locally through Ollama using an OpenAI-compatible API over 2,000 scored decision points. GPT-OSS-20B produces 100% valid JSON with zero malformed responses. Its overall score is 0.8008 in canonical mode and 0.7116 in interactive mode, a drop of 0.0892 points. The result shows that agent-coupled evaluation exposes compounding state consequences that fixed-trajectory evaluation structurally misses.

title: The Demand-Validation Paradox: Governing AI Ecosystems When Evidence Is Endogenous
affiliations: Indian Institute of Management Raipur and Indian Institute of Management Visakhapatnam

detail.title: The Demand-Validation Paradox: Governing AI Ecosystems When Evidence Is Endogenous

detail.abstract: AI governance increasingly depends on ecosystem signals, including demand, usage, safety, legitimacy, and risk, that are produced within the same digital relationships being governed. We develop a theory of evidence-reflexive digital ecosystem governance, showing how resource coupling can make these signals endogenous. A supported commitment may appear as demand or risk reduction before independent actors validate it. The same coupling creates an ethical and institutional dilemma: it can widen beneficial access and innovation while weakening the independent judgment needed to assess public exposure and accountability. We formalize this mechanism with a sequential provider-recipient-governor model and derive the demandvalidation gap. The model identifies when provenance separation or institutional safeguards are warranted by weighing coordination surplus, ethical exposure, verification value, induced coupling, and implementation cost. The gap connects algorithmic transparency, regulatory legibility, and market accountability by showing whether visible ecosystem claims can be independently interpreted and responsibly attributed. We frame ethics, regulation, and policy as one institutional design problem and make the theory inspectable through a cohesive SupTech framework: a source-audited network module maps resource influence and accountability, while a policy simulator translates institutional validation capacity into an actionable governance threshold. AI compute motivates the analysis, but the mechanism generalizes across digital ecosystems.

detail.abstract: This paper proposes a theoretical-formal model of the emergence, amplification, retention, and behavioral conversion of a sign's emotional capital. The starting thesis is that a logo can become a mediator between a person and a product and can transfer human properties to that product. In the proposed architecture, this thesis is decomposed into a sequence of testable links: visual structure of the sign → automatic extraction of mathematical shape descriptors → matrix of computational dissimilarities → space reconstructed by Multidimensional Scaling (MDS) → Euclidean distance to a human reference → anthropomorphic mediation → immediate affective response → scalar emotional capital → observable behavioral or market outcome.

title: Digital Financial Inclusion, Financing Constraints, and Corporate Investment Efficiency: Evidence from Chinese Listed Firms
affiliations: Sichuan University

detail.title: Digital Financial Inclusion, Financing Constraints, and Corporate Investment Efficiency: Evidence from Chinese Listed Firms
detail.abstract: This paper investigates whether the deepening of digital financial inclusion in China alleviates financing constraints and improves the investment efficiency of listed firms over the period 2016-2026. Using a balanced panel of 350 A-share non-financial firms matched with the prefecture-city Peking University Digital Financial Inclusion Index (DFII), we estimate two-way fixed-effects models in which the dependent variable is the absolute residual from a Richardson (2006) investment expectation model. A one-standard-deviation increase in city-level DFII is associated with a 12.4% reduction in investment inefficiency relative to the sample mean; the effect is present in both the over-investment and the under-investment sub-samples. The Hadlock-Pierce SA financing-constraint index amplifies the DFII effect: a negative and statistically significant DFII x SA interaction indicates that digital finance is most valuable for firms that are ex ante most financially constrained. Results survive two-step system GMM, a 2SLS design that instruments DFII with the long distance from each city to Hangzhou (Ant Financials’ headquarters), a propensity-score matched difference-in-differences design around the 2019 fintech-supervision reform, a placebo test, entropy balancing, exclusion of the COVID years, alternative winsorization, and an alternative dependent-variable measure (net new investment). Heterogeneity tests document stronger effects for non-state-owned, high-tech, coastal, and highly-constrained firms. Mechanism tests support three transmission channels: a lower cost of debt, a higher bank-loan share, and reduced reliance on trade credit. The evidence suggests that digital-finance infrastructure is a first-order determinant of capital-allocation efficiency in the world's second-largest economy.

detail.abstract: International market entry involves not only which markets to serve but also when to enter them, yet the timing implications of cross-national distance remain poorly understood. This paper examines how economic and geographic distance shape the timing of foreign market entry and how these effects differ between multinationals from developed and emerging economies. We theorize that both distance dimensions entail offsetting costs and benefits whose relative importance shifts with distance: low distance facilitates efficiency and knowledge transfer, moderate distance amplifies adaptation costs without commensurate advantages, and high distance can create arbitrage opportunities, competitive insulation, and access to strategic assets. Using a sample of 327 entries by 36 international telecom operators into 112 mobile broadband markets worldwide, results show significant inverted U-shaped effects of both economic and geographic distance on entry timing. The curvature is stronger for companies from developed economies compared to entrants from emerging economies. The study extends nonlinear distance research to entry timing, identifies firm origin as a boundary condition for distance-timing effects, and introduces a methodological template for more credible estimation of distance effects. Managerially, the findings challenge the view that distant markets should always be entered later, indicating instead that both very proximate and very distant markets may warrant early entry, whereas intermediate-distance markets pose the greatest timing challenges.

title: Complementing Traditional Human-Subject Surveys with LLM-Based Observational Surveys: A Use Case in Developing and Testing Dependency on GenAI
affiliations: , Rawls College of Business, Baylor University and Baylor University - Hankamer School of Business

detail.title: Complementing Traditional Human-Subject Surveys with LLM-Based Observational Surveys: A Use Case in Developing and Testing Dependency on GenAI

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract:
Traditional human-subject surveys are a cornerstone of Information Systems (IS) research for testing theoretical frameworks involving socio-technical and psychological constructs, yet their reliance on researcher-elicited and self-reported data introduces well-known limitations. Is there an approach to utilize the rich observational data to examine the carefully developed, multi-construct theoretical framework that is often tested by a traditional survey? Leveraging the semantic reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLM), we develop the method of LLM-based observational survey (LOS), a complementary research design to traditional survey design that operationalizes theoretically grounded constructs from naturally occurring digital traces. Whereas emerging LLM-based annotation approaches primarily use LLMs to classify or measure individual constructs, LOS moves LLMs from a tool for annotating data to an integral component of research design. Specifically, LOS translates the entire theory-testing architecture of a traditional survey (including sampling logic, construct definitions, measurement items, temporal structure, hypothesized relationships, and empirical estimation) into an observational design based on naturally occurring digital traces. By interpreting heterogeneous natural-language expressions against theoretically specified construct definitions and measurement semantics, LLMs enable multi-construct theory testing that would be difficult to accomplish using conventional text-analytic approaches. LOS thus provides a distinct and complementary pathway for examining theoretical frameworks without directly eliciting responses from research participants. 

We demonstrate LOS by examining how generative AI (GenAI) usage influences users' broader life outcomes. Drawing on technology dependency theory, we theorize two mediating pathways: functional dependency, reflecting reliance on GenAI for task execution and decision support, and emotional dependency, reflecting psychological attachment to GenAI for social and emotional support. We test the same theoretical framework using a two-wave human-subject survey of 290 GenAI users and an aligned LOS based on naturally occurring posts and comments from Reddit users. The two designs yield largely convergent evidence despite fundamentally different sampling and measurement processes. Our demonstration validates the potential of LOS to complement traditional surveys with observational evidence and reveals important tradeoffs in construct observability and LLM-based measurement. Our study broadens the methodological toolkit for theory testing in IS research and illustrates a new form of inquiry made possible by human-AI collaboration.
