detail.abstract: This research paper seeks to establish the reasons why luxury fashion brands are increasingly engaging the services of professional football celebrities to act as brand ambassadors and how marketing during football games leads to significant revenue generation for the fashion brands. In conducting the research, the writer was able to establish that the endorsement of luxury brands by football celebrities opens up significant opportunities for brand reach to young people, along with high numbers of followers on social media platforms, surpassing 800 million followers across the top footballers. It is agreed that the return on investment for football sponsorship stands between 10-15%, more than other forms of advertising, with some brands accruing up to $2.1 million in earned media value from a single footballer sponsorship. Furthermore, FIFA marketing has been seen to yield extraordinary high returns for the football industry, with the 2026 World Cup expected to yield returns amounting to 11 billion dollars, including marketing and sponsorship worth 2.7 billion dollars. Key psychological factors driving success include credibility transfer, emotional connection through shared cultural moments, and the match-up hypothesis where athlete image aligns with luxury brand values. This paper concludes that football celebrity partnerships represent a strategic evolution in luxury marketing, offering measurable financial returns alongside enhanced brand perception among digitally-native consumers.

title: The AI-Enhanced CMO: Redefining Strategic Leadership and Decision-making Authority in Marketing
affiliations: and Management and Science University (MSU)

detail.title: The AI-Enhanced CMO: Redefining Strategic Leadership and Decision-making Authority in Marketing

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: The authors received no specific funding for this work.

detail.abstract:
Background
This study investigates the influence of AI adoption in marketing strategic decision-making on
Chief Marketing Officer (CMO) strategic leadership effectiveness, with leadership agility as a
mediating variable. The proliferation of AI technologies has fundamentally altered the scope of
senior marketing leadership, repositioning CMOs as strategic architects of data-driven growth. Yet
the mechanisms through which AI adoption translates into elevated CMO strategic effectiveness
remain theoretically and empirically underdeveloped. Drawing on Upper Echelons Theory and
Dynamic Capabilities Theory, this study proposes and tests a mediation model in which leadership
agility serves as the explanatory mechanism.
Objective
The aim of this study is to examine how AI adoption in marketing strategic decision-making
influences CMO strategic leadership effectiveness, and to investigate the mediating role of
leadership agility.
Problem Statement
Despite the recent increase in the study of AI adoption in marketing and its influence on the role
of CMO’s. These studies have largely developed in isolation of each other. Little is known about
the way in which AI adoption translates it into tangible leadership outcome on senior marketing
level.
Research Gap
The AI adoption bringing a change in the CMO’s effectiveness is not studied empirically and the
impact of leadership agility in being a catalyst is also under-explored. This study provide a
mediation model which is empirically validated and gives insight into leveraging AI investment in
senior marketing leadership.
Methods
A quantitative cross-sectional survey of 300 senior marketing professionals was conducted, and
data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, frequency analysis, Cronbach's alpha reliability
analysis, principal axis factor analysis, Pearson correlation analysis, regression analysis, and
Hayes' PROCESS Macro mediation analysis.
Results
Findings confirm that AI adoption significantly predicts both leadership agility (β = .341, p < .001)
and CMO strategic leadership effectiveness (β = .616, p < .001), and that leadership agility
significantly predicts CMO strategic leadership effectiveness (β = .594, p < .001). Mediation
analysis reveals a statistically significant indirect effect of AI adoption on CMO effectiveness
through leadership agility (Effect = .112, 95% CI [.074, .153]), confirming partial mediation.
These findings have important implications for the strategic positioning of CMOs in AI-driven
organizations.
Conclusion
This study validates a mediation model linking AI adoption, leadership agility, and CMO strategic
effectiveness using data from 300 senior marketing professionals. All hypotheses were supported,
with the model explaining 54.6% of variance in CMO effectiveness. Organizations should invest
in both AI infrastructure and leadership agility development to maximize CMO strategic impact.

detail.abstract: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) has become a defining force that is driving a change in the marketing approach and transformations in organisations. The study investigated the relationship between the use of AI in marketing strategic decision-making (AIMSM) and the digital transformation (DT), with the effect of technological readiness (TR) being moderated. Primary data were gathered from 350 survey respondents, comprising marketing managers, digital marketing executives, business analysts, and AI-driven marketing and digital transformation professionals, using a quantitative cross-sectional survey design. On the basis of the TOE framework and Digital Transformation theory, relationships between AIMSM and three DT dimensions (digital process integration (DPI), data-driven marketing (DDM), and customer experience automation (CXA)) were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results indicated that AIMSM had a significant positive effect on DPI (p < 0.001), while its effects on DDM and CXA were not statistically significant. Regarding moderation, TR significantly strengthened the relationships between AIMSM and DDM (p = 0.012) and DPI (p = 0.001), which shows the high contribution of TR with AIMSM and DT dimensions. The results of this study provided direction to the organizations that they would need to have a solid technological basis, trained staff, and willingness to obtain meaningful and desirable DT results. The originality of this study lies in its understanding of how AIMSM leads to DT via DPI, DDM, and CXA, and highlights how TR is conditionally significant in the successful transformation enabled by AI.

detail.abstract: Background. Commentary on professional services websites is drawn almost entirely from agency casework, a sample composed of firms that had already decided their website mattered enough to pay someone about it. The UK accountancy profession is one of the few sectors whose regulators publish searchable practice registers, making a properly drawn sample possible. Methods. We audited the public websites of 494 UK accountancy practices drawn from the published ACCA and ICAEW practice registers, sampled with probability proportional to size across twelve UK regions and measured with a single instrument over 1 and 2 September 2026. The frame covers those two registers in the United Kingdom only: AAT-licensed practices, members in practice of other accountancy bodies, unlicensed bookkeepers and independent financial advisers were outside it, and no finding is offered as describing them. Thirty-six website faults were recorded per firm alongside platform, page count and region. Two interpretive check families were validated blind against 213 passages from 42 firms held out of all earlier development. Prevalence is reported with Wilson intervals; pairwise association was tested by Fisher's exact test and then re-tested under Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel stratification by site-size quartile, with Benjamini-Hochberg correction throughout. Results. Obtaining 494 usable firms required drawing 926 domains, an attrition rate of 46.7 per cent. Faults divide into two families with opposite relationships to site size: omission, commonest on the smallest sites, and neglect, commonest on the largest. Platform predicts technical condition more strongly than any deliberate choice measured, with sitemap absence at 0 per cent on one platform, 15 per cent on another and 55 per cent on bespoke builds. Of 53 pairwise associations significant in a first analysis, 38 did not survive stratification by size, and stratification revealed two the first analysis had missed. Two firms in 494 state an anti-money-laundering supervisor, a near-null result confirmed by two blind raters reading 34 candidate passages. Conclusions. Most recorded faults were preventable by specification rather than by audit. Platform defaults determine more of a website's technical condition than intent, including in machine-readability, where 17.8 per cent of firms publish an llms.txt file that almost none of them chose to publish. The instrument's own error rate is reported alongside every finding, and is the reason no firm is identified.

title: Competing for Commoditization or Platforming for De-commoditization: The Role of Salient Thinking
affiliations: University of Science and Technology of China (USTC) - School of Management, Purdue University - Department of Consumer Sciences and Retailing and Hebei University of Technology

detail.title: Competing for Commoditization or Platforming for De-commoditization: The Role of Salient Thinking

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA
declarations.funderStatement: NA

detail.abstract: Consumer preferences are often context-dependent, with attention naturally drawn to a product's most prominent attribute. Applying the behavioral framework of "salient thinking," this paper examines how firms strategically design channel architecture to manipulate consumer focus. We reveal a fundamental asymmetry in the incentives for firms to transition from direct competitors to cooperative complementors. Under direct competition, markets often devolve into a "commoditized," price-salient equilibrium. However, we demonstrate that relative product quality allows firms to escape this trap. When a lower-quality firm resells a premium competitor's product, the resulting contrast shifts consumer focus from price to quality; this "de-commoditization" fosters a market environment that can overcome double marginalization, particularly when quality-production costs remain moderate. Crucially, this mechanism is structurally asymmetric: it fails if the high-quality firm acts as the reseller, as low-quality firms prefer price-salient competition. These insights provide a novel, cognitiondriven rationale for why premium and budget brands selectively co-locate in modern retail ecosystems.

title: Mechanism Design with Qualitative Demand Information: A Posted Price or a Price Lottery?
affiliations: , Hong Kong University of Science & Technology (HKUST) - Department of Information Systems, Business Statistics and Operations Management,  and Shanghai University of Finance and Economics - School of Information Management and Engineering

detail.title: Mechanism Design with Qualitative Demand Information: A Posted Price or a Price Lottery?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no competing financial or personal interests that could have influenced this study.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Qualitative information about the shape of customer valuations can materially affect selling decisions even when the distribution is not fully specified. We study a seller of an indivisible good to a privately informed buyer with value in a bounded interval. The seller knows that the distribution satisfies moment restrictions and belongs to a prescribed shape class, and evaluates incentive-compatible and individually rational mechanisms by worst-case expected revenue. We use a generator-based framework that represents shape-restricted distributions as mixtures of generators and mechanisms as lotteries over posted prices. The resulting primal-dual characterization links active prices to binding demand scenarios in a worst-case distribution. Qualitative information affects both the revenue guarantee and the form of the selling mechanism. Under unimodality with known mean and mode, the optimal mechanism exhibits three possible forms: a posted price, a hybrid mechanism, or an upper-tail price lottery. Under symmetric mean-variance information, increasing dispersion moves the optimal policy from randomized markdowns to midpoint posted pricing and then to randomized premiums. The seller's pricing emphasis shifts from coverage to baseline protection and then to margin extraction, so greater dispersion does not simply imply higher prices or greater mechanism complexity. Under decreasing-convex information, a lower mean moves the policy from a posted price to a two-point price lottery, with numerical results indicating richer randomization at still lower means. Across the characterized cases, a single binding adverse scenario supports pricing simplicity, whereas competing scenarios can make randomization valuable as a hedge against demand ambiguity.

title: Strategic Summarization in Product Search
affiliations: and Hong Kong University of Science & Technology (HKUST) - Department of Marketing

detail.title: Strategic Summarization in Product Search

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: This research is funded by Research Grants Council of Hong Kong under the scheme of General Research Fund.

detail.abstract: As consumers leave more product reviews, the amount of product information grows and so does the need for a preview of the information. We examine when a summary should be introduced, and if so, how informative it should be, given its influence on consumers' continual information acquisition and eventual purchase behaviors. We present a tractable model to capture consumers' optimal search behavior and the optimal summary design of a firm. Because a summary is a coarsened version of the original review information, it introduces correlated learning: reading a summary not only shifts product belief ("belief-shifting channel"), but also reveals what to expect about the review information ("predictive channel"). We find that a summary need not increase product conversion: when consumers are optimistic, an unfavorable summary can divert them from direct purchase; and when they are weakly pessimistic, it can discourage them from continual information acquisition. For the purpose of maximizing purchase rate, a summary is useful only when consumers hold weakly optimistic or pessimistic priors. In these belief regions, the optimal informativeness depends on whether the summary serves as a vote of confidence, where a favorable preview induces purchase and an unfavorable one triggers further review reading, a benefit of the doubt, where a favorable preview cannot induce purchase but makes the reviews worth reading, or is all the consumer needs, who makes the decision without reading the review.

title: The Consequences of Consumer Engagement in Social Networking Sites
affiliations: Anadolu University

detail.title: The Consequences of Consumer Engagement in Social Networking Sites

detail.abstract: Consumer engagement is increasingly becoming one of the important issues in the competitive business environment. Both researches and practitioners are focusing on how consumer engagement can be enhanced through different channels. The emergence of social networks has significantly caused a shift in consumer behaviors and brand relationships. With its unique features and structure, Social Networking Sites (SNS) offer an upper advantage to build consumer brand relationships and instant consumer engagement. Although researchers and practitioners are giving so much importance to consumer engagement, there is still a need to understand how engagement affects consumer behavior. Therefore, this study set out to determine the consequences of consumer engagement in SNS. It further viewed consumer engagement as a multi-dimensional concept comprising behavioral, cognitive and emotional dimensions and as such the hypotheses were aimed at determining how each of the three dimensions of consumer engagement affect the individual consequences of consumer engagement such as brand loyalty, satisfaction, commitment and trust in SNS. The study used a quantitative research design and developed a model that was based on the hypotheses developedfor the study. It used a questionnaire survey to collect data from Anadolu University students in summer school. Facebook is chosen as a case for this study. 400 questionnaires were collected and the analyses were conducted with the 387 valid questionnaire. The research data was analyzed by SPSS program 20.0 version. The results suggest that emotional and behavioral consumer engagement dimensions were significant predictors for brand loyalty; emotional consumer engagement for satisfaction, cognitive and behavioral consumer engagement for commitment, while behavioral and emotional engagement dimensions were found to be significant predictors for trust. In sum, the study suggests brand loyalty, satisfaction, commitment, and trust to be possible consequences of consumer engagement in an online platform such as Facebook in our case.

title: To What Extent do Cognitive Biases Affect Consumer Decisionmaking Under Uncertainty?

detail.title: To What Extent do Cognitive Biases Affect Consumer Decisionmaking Under Uncertainty?

declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required for this study. No human participants or identifiable personal data were involved.

detail.abstract: Consumer decision-making under uncertainty represents a critical area of inquiry in behavioral marketing research. Traditional rational choice models often fail to capture the complexity of real-world choices, particularly when individuals face ambiguous product attributes, incomplete information, and unpredictable outcomes. This study investigates the extent to which cognitive biases influence consumer decisions in uncertain environments, focusing on mechanisms through which heuristic-driven judgments shape preferences, risk perception, and purchase intentions. Drawing on insights from behavioral economics, prospect theory, and cognitive psychology, a conceptual framework is proposed wherein cognitive biases mediate the relationship between environmental uncertainty and decision-making outcomes. Using a survey-based methodology with a sample of 400 consumers, structural equation modeling (SEM) was employed to test hypothesized relationships and examine the interaction effects of multiple biases. Findings indicate that higher levels of uncertainty increase reliance on cognitive biases, which in turn significantly affect consumer choice behavior. Notably, interactions among biases amplify deviations from rational predictions, highlighting the compounded influence of heuristic-driven judgments. These results provide both theoretical contributions, by integrating cognitive biases into decision-making models under uncertainty, and practical implications for marketers, who can design interventions to mitigate adverse bias effects and support more informed consumer choices.

title: Signaling through Search Assistance: The Strategic Display of AI-generated Overview
affiliations: University of Science and Technology of China, University of Science and Technology of China (USTC) and

detail.title: Signaling through Search Assistance: The Strategic Display of AI-generated Overview

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NO
declarations.funderStatement: NO

detail.abstract: Search platforms are increasingly deploying AI-generated overview (AIGO) features to help consumers evaluate search results before clicking. Beyond reducing search effort, AIGO display serves an informational role: platforms condition display on private assessments of query-link match quality, enabling consumers to draw inferences from both display and non-display. We develop a signaling-game model in which a platform privately observes a signal about query-link match quality and decides whether to display a costly AIGO before consumers decide whether to click. Display lowers consumers' inspection cost, while the display decision shapes their posterior beliefs about match quality. Our findings are threefold. First, the platform implements AIGO only when its generation cost is sufficiently low and consumers face moderate inspection cost. When inspection cost is low, consumers are already inclined to click without AIGO; when it is high, they remain reluctant to click even with AIGO. Second, conditional on adoption, AIGO deployment changes qualitatively with inspection cost. The platform first displays AIGO primarily after unfavorable signals to stimulate marginal clicks among consumers who would otherwise not click; then displays AIGO after both signals to capture incremental clicks across signal states; and eventually displays AIGO primarily after favorable signals to preserve clicking incentives as weaker matches become unresponsive. Third, AIGO adoption generates gains for the platform and for consumers in aggregate, but distributes surplus unevenly across underlying match states. Consumers facing high-quality matches benefit throughout the adoption region, whereas those facing low-quality matches may lose surplus when inspection cost is high because AIGO display can mislead them into clicking. These findings suggest that AIGO should be managed as a selective deployment instrument rather than a default interface upgrade, with platform managers and policymakers accounting for its efficiency and informational effects on consumers as well as its distributional welfare consequences across search contexts.

title: Control without Ownership: Public Insurance, Firm Boundaries, and Buyer Authority in Fixed-Factor Supply Chains
affiliations: Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU)

detail.title: Control without Ownership: Public Insurance, Firm Boundaries, and Buyer Authority in Fixed-Factor Supply Chains
detail.abstract: Public support can change not only who receives income but also who controls productive assets. I study a fixed-factor supply chain in which private state-contingent finance is costly or capacity constrained and owners choose among autonomy, contractual control, and integration. A general theorem for finite-state convex transfer technologies decomposes the policy effect on contractual-control value into state-solvency relief and the participation value of the gap between contractual and autonomous marginal support. A common-primitives two-state specialization gives closed-form sufficient conditions for ownership-control divergence and verifies them on an open parameter region. Under single crossing, support can reduce legal integration while increasing downstream protocol authority. A second-price buyer-menu mechanism separates buyer-form allocation from post-selection surplus division. Organizational change alters the recipient base and optimal support under a grant-like policy. A separate emergency-loan application illustrates repayable public liquidity. Private claim completion can eliminate the organizational effect.

title: Male Dominance and Cultural Extinction
affiliations: University of Bristol - Department of Economics and University of California, Merced - Department of Economics

detail.title: Male Dominance and Cultural Extinction
detail.abstract: Why do some cultures go extinct while others prevail? In this paper, we show that a society's risk of cultural extinction, proxied by language loss, is shaped by its ancestral gender norms and by how these norms differ from those of competing cultures. Using the Ethnologue and the Male Dominance Index for a global sample of languages, we start by showing that languages from more gender-equal societies face a higher likelihood of extinction than those from male-dominant societies. We propose a conceptual framework in which male-dominant societies are more expansionist via two channels: (i) military capacity sustained through surplus extraction, and (ii) demographic pressure through women's specialization in domestic and reproductive labor. As a result, they expand at the expense of more gender-egalitarian groups. We test this prediction in two empirical settings. Leveraging European colonization as a natural experiment, we find that Indigenous societies with more gender-equal norms than their colonizers are more vulnerable to cultural extinction. We examine alternative pre-colonial societal arrangements and find that cultural extinction is best explained by asymmetries in male dominance rather than in hierarchy or dominance more broadly. Exploiting local variation in neighboring groups' gender structure across Africa, we further show that languages from gender-egalitarian societies are less likely to survive in grid cells located close to male-dominant neighbors, with military capacity and population pressure predicting language expansion across the continent.

title: Residence for Corporate Income Tax Purposes - General Report
affiliations: International Bureau of Fiscal Documentation

detail.title: Residence for Corporate Income Tax Purposes - General Report

publicationDetails.detailsText: International Fiscal Association 2025 Lisbon Congress | cahiers volume 109

detail.abstract:
Residence is one of the most fundamental legal concepts for taxation. This general report aims to provide a better understanding of the function, meaning and role performed by the concept in modern corporate income tax systems. A comprehensive assessment of the branch reports reveals a complex normative landscape shaped by globalisation and digitalisation and evolving legal concepts under a mist of indeterminacy. Regarding domestic law, there is considerable diversity, with divergent jurisdictional approaches, encompassing the interplay of incorporation, governance and other criteria and with a clear trend of expanding the scope of the concept. At the income tax treaty level, while most treaties still adhere to place of effective management as a tie-breaker, there is a progressive shift to the mutual agreement procedure (hereinafter MAP), which should be regarded with concern. Such a mechanism, as it prevents taxpayers from anticipating the tax consequences of their (often genuine and needed) behaviour, is particularly worrisome, taking into account that residence is often a trigger for worldwide taxation.

The general report underscores the need for enhanced international cooperation and legislative reforms to address the challenges emphasised by globalisation and digitalisation, advocating for a nuanced balance between sovereignty and global tax fairness.

title: Natural Resources, Democracy, and Labour-Market Outcomes in the Public Sector
affiliations: University “G. d’Annunzio” Chieti Pescara and University of Verona - Department of Economics

detail.title: Natural Resources, Democracy, and Labour-Market Outcomes in the Public Sector
detail.abstract: Governments in resource-rich countries may use a sizable share of the revenue from their underground wealth to buy support through public employment. This occurs in both democratic governments (which need to be re-elected) and autocratic governments (which have to prevent riots and regime change). Using the Worldwide Bureaucracy Indicators dataset provided by the World Bank, we analyse the effect of natural resources on public employment in developing countries from 2000 to 2018. We find that resource rents may have an effect on public sector characteristics. However, uncovering the heterogeneous effects of different types of natural resources, we find that oil and gas wealth may increase public employment in countries that are not fully democratic, while forest wealth has a positive impact for all values of democracy. At the same time, the public sector wage premium is positively affected by oil and forest in non-democratic countries and by gas when the level of democracy is very high.

detail.abstract: This policy paper explores the intersection of behavioral economics and poverty, examining how psychological factors associated with scarcity perpetuate the cycle of poverty. The author discusses how individuals in poverty often focus on immediate needs, which hinders their ability to engage in long-term planning and decision-making. The paper highlights the impact of economic instability, particularly in the context of inflation and housing insecurity, on financial behavior. It emphasizes the importance of targeted interventions, such as microfinance programs and community-based support, that can empower individuals and disrupt the cycle of poverty. By analyzing successful models from various contexts, the paper advocates for the integration of behavioral insights into policy design to promote financial inclusion and enhance the effectiveness of poverty alleviation strategies. Ultimately, it calls for a more nuanced understanding of poverty that considers psychological dimensions and the need for collaborative solutions to foster economic equity.

detail.abstract:
Artificial intelligence is no longer the domain of large enterprises with extensive resources—it is increasingly accessible to businesses of all sizes, from solopreneurs to global corporations. Small Is Beautiful! How Businesses of Every Size Are Transforming Through AI examines how advances in AI tools and platforms are lowering barriers to entry, enabling organizations to enhance productivity, optimize operations, and compete more effectively. Across diverse use cases—from individual entrepreneurs automating workflows to small businesses improving customer engagement and larger firms scaling intelligent systems—the paper demonstrates that AI adoption is becoming a practical and strategic imperative across the entire business landscape.

The paper explores how AI capabilities manifest differently depending on organizational scale, operational complexity, and regional context. It highlights how solopreneurs leverage AI as a digital partner to extend capacity, how small companies adopt cost-effective tools to improve efficiency and customer experience, and how medium and large enterprises integrate AI into core systems to drive performance, innovation, and governance. It further examines how regulatory environments, data infrastructure, and market maturity shape AI implementation globally, emphasizing that while core principles are consistent, execution must be context-specific.

The paper outlines a set of implementation strategies for effective AI adoption, including starting with targeted use cases, ensuring data readiness, investing in workforce skills, and embedding governance, ethics, and compliance into AI systems. It emphasizes the importance of phased adoption, measurable outcomes, and continuous evaluation, alongside the need for flexibility as technologies evolve. Ultimately, the paper positions AI as a “great leveler,” arguing that success depends less on organizational size and more on strategic clarity, responsible deployment, and the ability to integrate AI into long-term business transformation.

detail.abstract:
AI is shifting from a predominantly centralized model, controlled by a fewdominant players, toward a hybrid landscape that incorporates decentralizednetworks of autonomous agents.NANDA (Networked Agents and Decentralized AI) is a pioneering open protocoldesigned to establish an actual “Internet of AI Agents,” enabling autonomous AIsystems to interact, transact, and collaborate across decentralized networks—much like the Domain Name System (DNS) revolutionized the early web.NANDA provides an open network for the discovery of AI agents, a trust framework with credentials, and a collaborative ecosystem.By building on Anthropic’s Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Google’s Agent-toAgent Protocol (A2A), NANDA extends these frameworks to allow businesses andindustries to leverage interoperable, intelligent AI systems without reliance ontraditional control constraints such as centralized gatekeepers, siloed platforms,limited discoverability, and opaque trust models.As AI advances, focusing only on centralized models isn’t enough—AI mustbecome autonomous, enabling agents to work efficiently across industriesand ecosystems. This paper explores the business implications, governancechallenges, and strategic opportunities associated with NANDA and the rise ofthe Agentic Economy.

title: Key Determinants of Warehouse Management System (WMS) Implementation in Logistics Service Providers (LSPs) in Malaysia

detail.title: Key Determinants of Warehouse Management System (WMS) Implementation in Logistics Service Providers (LSPs) in Malaysia

declarations.funderStatement: Self Funded

detail.abstract: This study investigates the key determinants influencing Warehouse Management System (WMS) implementation among Logistics Service Providers (LSPs) in Malaysia. Although WMS implementation can enhance warehouse efficiency, operational effectiveness, information visibility, and overall business performance, limited empirical research has examined the factors influencing WMS implementation among Malaysian LSPs. Drawing on the Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) framework, this study examines seven determinants of WMS implementation: technology cost, technology compatibility, organizational readiness, top management support, organizational size, competitive pressure, and government support. Data were collected through a questionnaire survey involving 256 logistics companies in Malaysia and analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings indicate that technological, organizational, and environmental factors significantly influence WMS implementation among Malaysian LSPs. The study provides empirical evidence on the key determinants of WMS implementation and highlights the importance of organizational capabilities, technological considerations, and external environmental factors in supporting successful implementation. The findings offer practical implications for logistics managers in developing effective WMS implementation strategies and provide useful insights for policymakers seeking to encourage digital technology adoption and enhance the competitiveness of Malaysia's logistics sector.

detail.abstract: The global conversation on carbon credits has been constrained by a narrowperspective that severely limits their transformative potential. Too often, theseinstruments are treated as simple accounting tools for offsetting emissions.This reductionist view fails to recognize that carbon credits should bepositioned within broader planetary health strategies, functioning as integralcomponents of systems designed to restore ecological wellness. Likehealthcare, carbon credits should prioritize systemic planetary health oversymptom-level offsets.This article reimagines carbon credits as catalysts for co-evolution, usingblockchain technology to verify and support practices like community-ledreforestation and Indigenous stewardship, thereby aligning human andecological systems. By moving beyond narrow criteria for project selectiontoward regenerative partnerships rooted in the ecological and cultural realitiesof each location, carbon markets can better drive social and climate progress.This means working not only in place but with place, treating it as a livingsystem capable of evolution.The current framing of carbon credits is plagued by mistrust in accounting,unequal distribution of benefits, and insufficient impact on emissions. This systemic dysfunction demands fundamental rethinking, not minoradjustments. Our proposed shift represents more than idealism; it provides apractical framework for addressing the interconnected social, economic, andecological aspects of value creation. We also argue that blockchain can serveas a key enabler of this transformation. Harnessing this technology allows us tobuild transparent, efficient, and inclusive carbon markets that align economi cincentives with both social equity and ecological regeneration.

detail.abstract: This paper examines fiscal prudence during Narendra Modi's administrations in Gujarat and at the Union level using comparative fiscal indicators, debt accounting and documentary evidence. In Gujarat, three-year averages show a 1.17 percentage-point improvement in the revenue balance relative to state output, a 0.69-point reduction in the fiscal deficit and a 0.29-point increase in capital outlay. The primary deficit rose modestly, from 0.30 to 0.45 percent. Substantial fiscal improvement combined revenue-account strengthening, lower interest absorption and greater capital spending; favourable interest-growth dynamics drove the decline in the debt ratio. These gains occurred within a wider state consolidation. Electricity reform connects collection discipline and service restructuring to continuing budgetary support. The Union record comprises consolidation through 2018-19, a policy and revenue reversal in 2019-20, and substantial post-pandemic adjustment accompanied by higher capital expenditure. Liabilities remained above their pre-pandemic level, while the operational debt objective moved to a higher ratio and later date. The evidence establishes substantial fiscal improvement in Gujarat's finances and a more uneven Union record, whose strongest result is the scale and expenditure composition of post-pandemic consolidation.

detail.abstract: Special-purpose governments are a defining feature of American local governance, accounting for the largest share of local governments, yet we know surprisingly little about how organizational separation changes the exercise of administrative authority. This article examines that question through crisis response. Using Public Libraries Survey data from seven states, we compare independently governed library districts with libraries embedded in city and county governments before and during the COVID-19 emergency. In FY2020, the adjusted probability that library staff were reassigned to non-library government or nonprofit functions was 5.4 percent in library districts and 11.1 percent in embedded libraries, a relative difference of 51 percentage points. A common six-state interaction model shows that this gap was significantly smaller in FY2021 and FY2022. Library districts also experienced about one fewer week of physical closure during FY2020-FY2021, although state-level inference for that result is weaker. Districts did not show a broad advantage in total staffing, service adaptation, or routine network connectedness. The administrative difference was concentrated in cross-functional staff use during the acute phase of the crisis, which is consistent with organizational separation limiting the reach of administrative authority when competing claims on resources intensify.

title: Strong Formulations for Multi-State Unit Commitment with Transition-Specific Timing Requirements

detail.title: Strong Formulations for Multi-State Unit Commitment with Transition-Specific Timing Requirements

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have influenced the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was supported by NGF – GroenvermogenNL 2022 (grant number NGF.1611.22.021).

detail.abstract: Modern sustainable energy systems increasingly rely on assets such as hydrogen electrolyzers, fuel cells, and storage-coupled converters, which operate in multiple states and face transition-specific timing requirements. Unit commitment (UC) provides a standard optimization framework for discrete operating decisions, and its polyhedral theory covers two-state on/off logic with minimum up/down times, which impose post-transition persistence at the state level. However, a distinct structure arises when transition eligibility depends on how long a unit has continuously occupied its source state, so that arcs leaving one state can carry different requirements. We introduce an arc-specific predecessor-residency logic for this structure that separates pre-transition preparation from post-transition persistence and accommodates asymmetric timing requirements and immediately eligible transitions. We develop a compact multi-state UC formulation and an ideal state-residency extension, a unit-flow model on an acyclic time-expanded network, whose projection is exactly the compact integer hull for arbitrary finite transition graphs under a common initial-history convention. For the three-state case, we determine the dimension of the hull with an unrestricted initial state, characterize which of its principal inequalities are facet-defining, and derive aggregated eligibility inequalities that strengthen the compact relaxation. In a hydrogen-integrated electricity application, modeling standby raises hydrogen-side net profit by about 31% for the same hydrogen volume and substantially reduces branch-and-cut effort relative to a two-state approximation.

detail.abstract: We examine voluntary disclosure incentives in one of the economy's most opaque environments, early-stage startups. Using a new dataset of startup-issued press releases, we study a theoretical equilibrium in which high-quality ventures remain "silent,'' while lower-quality ventures disclose information to attract new investors when their existing VCs are financially constrained. Consistent with this counter-signaling interpretation, firms issuing press releases are associated with lower follow-on financing rates, lower valuation returns, and slower near-term employee growth. Yet these firms also add more new investors and a more geographically diverse investor base. Press releases with more sentiment-heavy, subjective, and less readable language are associated with lower subsequent returns, consistent with a mix of promotional "spin'' and the disclosure of adverse content. The findings help explain why classical information-unraveling predictions may break down in entrepreneurial finance and highlight the strategic role of disclosure in shaping startup capital flows.

This opinion piece discusses the urgent need for a transformative approach to sustainability in the context of climate change. The author argues that traditional methods of integrating sustainability into business practices are insufficient, as evidenced by the ongoing rise in carbon emissions and biodiversity loss despite numerous international efforts. Instead, the paper advocates for a framework called Digital (d)GAIA 5.0, which encourages organizations to engage in narrative storytelling that emphasizes collective action towards achieving net-zero emissions and creating regenerative institutions.

The author highlights the historical disconnect between economic activities and ecological considerations, suggesting that capitalism can be harnessed as a force for sustainability rather than seen as an adversary. By aligning economic incentives with environmental stewardship, organizations can foster innovation and create shared value. The piece calls for a shift in mindset that prioritizes emotional engagement and behavioral change, urging leaders to adopt collaborative strategies that integrate advanced technologies like AI and blockchain to drive meaningful progress in sustainability efforts.

The paper concludes by emphasizing the importance of creating inclusive processes that empower all stakeholders to participate in the sustainability narrative, ultimately aiming for a harmonious balance between economic growth and ecological integrity.

detail.abstract: This study investigates how individual short-sighted decisions propagate systemic risks through resource constraints, information asymmetry, and dynamic strategic interactions. By extending the Three-Level Prisoner’s Decision Trap (PDP) framework, we propose a cross-level transmission mechanism linking micro-level myopia, meso-level path dependence, and macro-level equilibrium lock-in. Based on multi-case empirical analysis—including global electric vehicle partial failures and systemic risks; chinese youth's homebuying-resistance and real estate systemic risks; rural-urban labor return migration and economic fluctuation risks; deficiencies in social foundational safeguards and community relief systems; individual-organizational balance sheet recessions and systemic risks; entrepreneurs' and managers' operational decision-making and organizational systemic risks; as well as industrial chain disruptions with urban-rural institutional imbalances and trade friction risks—we quantify risk thresholds using the Systemic Risk Index (SRI) and validate its predictive efficacy via panel regression and system dynamics modeling. Key findings reveal that individual behaviors (e.g., high time discount rates, δ) amplify resource degradation and strategic rigidity, triggering cascading failures across sectors. Policy simulations demonstrate that targeted interventions (e.g., dynamic subsidies, debt restructuring) reduce SRI by 0.2–0.4. Theoretically, this research integrates behavioral economics and complex systems theory, offering dynamic tools to mitigate systemic vulnerabilities. Practically, it provides actionable strategies for policymakers and managers to balance innovation incentives and risk governance in rapidly evolving socio-economic systems.

detail.abstract: Renewable Energy Communities (RECs) are increasingly recognised as key instruments for a just energy transition. Yet evidence on their impact on households' energy behaviour remains limited. This study focuses on the Agra do Amial REC, located in a deprived neighbourhood in Porto, Portugal's second largest city, and assesses its impact on electricity consumption and expenditures. Using high-frequency (hourly/daily) data and a forecast-based counterfactual approach, we estimate the causal effect of REC participation. Results show an increase of electricity consumption and a net reduction in energy bills, consistent with improved access to essential energy services. These findings offer policy-relevant insights for the design of just and inclusive community-based energy models in Portugal.

title: Delisting Forensics: Governance Failure and a Public-Data Screen for Leveraged Looting on Korea's KOSDAQ

The screen is a screening instrument, not an adjudication: a high score means a firm's public record resembles patterns the Financial Supervisory Service itself publishes as investor red flags, not that any law was broken. detail.abstract: Korean regulators describe a recurring failure mode of the KOSDAQ market: the acquisition of a listed company with borrowed money rather than the acquirer's own capital, followed by tunneling of corporate assets and exit through the share price. We call the pattern leveraged looting, after Akerlof and Romer's (1993) looting. Enforcement is necessarily ex post. This paper asks how much of the pattern is visible ex ante in public data alone. From a project master of 3,948 firms we identify 1,185 that have left the Korea Exchange roster, recover the market segment of every one of them by triangulating three sources, and study the 723 KOSDAQ departures against 1,625 currently listed KOSDAQ firms. Coverage is the central obstacle and we measure it rather than assume it away: only 27% of departed firms have any audit-opinion filing in our collection, 15% an ownership-change filing, and 9% a convertible-bond filing, and we show that median imputation makes composite governance scores uninformative for exactly this population — 70.8% of departed firms collapse into the middle grade. On the subsamples where measurement exists, departed firms differ sharply: 33.7% carry at least one non-clean audit opinion against 2.8% of listed peers; a governance-incident behaviour score is 13 points higher at the median (p < 0.001); and repeated control transfers are twice as prevalent among firms with any recorded change. A five-criterion screen that translates the Financial Supervisory Service's published red flags into disclosure-based indicators flags 78 of 723 departures (10.8%), with 27 firms (3.7%) at the highest tier. Run on the 1,625 listed comparators with identical definitions, and conditioning both groups on having any audit filing, the screen flags 39.8% of departed against 16.4% of listed firms (13.8% against 2.6% at the top tier); that separation is carried chiefly by the audit-opinion criterion, and the three criteria that precede the audit stage separate the groups only weakly. Balance-sheet tracing finds critical fund-outflow patterns — affiliate investment, loans and other receivables surging past a fifth of total assets — in 24 of those 27; parsed convertible-bond filings show 97.8% private placements, refixing clauses in half, one savings-bank group subscribing across seven issuers, and one issuer selling convertibles to 34 subscribers at a conversion price implying 87% dilution. The screened cohort's profile is directionally consistent with the enforcement statistics the FSS published after its 2019 joint inspection. All screened firms are anonymised: the screen is a triage instrument, not an adjudication. We close by mapping which provisions of Korea's 2025-2027 Commercial Act amendments reach the acquisition, extraction and exit stages of the playbook — and which of them, because of the KRW 2 trillion asset threshold, never reach the segment of the market where the pattern lives.

detail.abstract: This paper asserts that organizational waste is a more pervasive and ultimately more destructive threat than identifiable fraud. Investigating sectors from healthcare to government, we unmask waste in the form of bureaucratic paralysis, exorbitant executive pay, and systemic resource misallocation. Leaders frequently betray their fiduciary duty by prioritizing short-term gains and public optics over responsible, long-term stewardship, a choice that jeopardizes organizational viability and stakeholders' interests. Fraud certainly relies on explicit deception. However, federal audit and fraud-loss data suggest that routine waste, driven by negligence or mismanagement, poses a far graver ethical failure. Waste systematically erodes effectiveness and breaches our moral obligation to steward resources wisely for current and future generations. The paper calls for decisive action, advocating for radical oversight mechanisms, such as appointing waste-prevention officers, to combat this insidious drain on value.

detail.abstract: The role of corporations in society is again the subject of debate across finance, law, and management. This essay aims to expand the debate beyond whether social benefits and costs be included in the corporation's objective function. I make the following two arguments. First, corporate purpose is broader than the debate recognizes. It is a mechanism for social choice, defining which problems a firm takes up, which solutions it pursues, whose interests count, and how conflicts among them are adjudicated. Purpose thereby shapes the admissible domain of corporate action, guides judgment among incommensurable alternatives, and helps form an organizational constituency capable of acting on that ordering. Second, polarization creates a larger divergence in values across the population, reducing consensus on the social issues raised by the modern economy. The appropriate locus of social choice-and therefore the appropriate scope of corporate purpose-depends on both the breadth of the parties materially affected and the degree of contestation over the end. Purpose has its greatest capacity and legitimacy within bounded constituencies, while broad and contested effects call for government and the political process. Revisiting the institutional settlement that emerged from the debates of the 1930s, the essay presents corporate purpose and public authority as complementary institutions for governing modern capitalism.

detail.abstract: INTRODUCTION : This study assesses the impact of goat farming training on the knowledge levels of tribal youth of Banswara district in Rajasthan state across nine critical production and marketing. Data was collected from 73 youth participants both before and after their training during the 2019-20 period, utilizing a quasi-experimental "difference-indifferences" approach for comparison. detail.abstract: In September 2025 Malaysia replaced a blanket petrol subsidy with a targeted one, xing the pump price at RM1.99 a litre for eligible citizens up to a monthly quota and charging the market price beyond it. Because the subsidised price is xed and the unsubsidised price is reset weekly, the subsidy per litre is not a policy parameter but a residual: over the scheme's rst 48 weeks it ranged from RM0.53 to RM2.28, a factor of 4.3, while the announced price never changed. The RM11 billion allocated for twelve months was spent in eight, and the overrun was almost entirely a price eect volume ran at 92 percent of the budgeted level while the per-litre gap averaged 1.7 times the RM0.61 the budget assumed. In April 2026 the quota was cut from 300 litres to 200, and in September restored, at a per-litre gap almost as high as when it was cut. That reversal matters for interpretation: the quota is the programme's most readily adjustable parameter, but it is not mechanically determined by the scal gap. The paper then asks who a quota cut reaches, and nds that the public record does not permit a unique estimate. Lowering a ceiling imposes no loss below the new level, a loss rising linearly between the new and old ceilings, and a constant loss only above the old one, so the disclosed shares identify how many people are exposed but not what they lose the distribution between 200 and 300 litres, which governs the answer, has never been published. Four threshold claims and one mean have been disclosed across three dierently worded reference populations, two of them giving 90 and 80 percent for the same 200-litre threshold seven weeks apart. Scaling the two disclosed shares by the eligibility count gives upper-bound exposure scenarios of 1.6 million and 3.2 million, though the two are not strictly comparable and the true gure is not recoverable. The distribution is not unmeasured: a deputy nance minister has described the scheme as providing data on Malaysians' travel patterns. It is unpublished.

title: Automation and Dynamic Efficiency: When Do Robots Benefit Every Generation?
affiliations: Tsinghua University - Tsinghua University School of Economics and Management, Princeton University, Tsinghua University - School of Economics & Management and Peking University HSBC Business School

detail.title: Automation and Dynamic Efficiency: When Do Robots Benefit Every Generation?
detail.abstract: We study the welfare consequences of automation in an overlapping-generations economy in which robots are both productive inputs and assets through which young households save. When automation substitutes for labor and compresses wages, a marginal improvement in robot technology benefits every generation if and only if the pre-robot economy is dynamically inefficient; once robots are in use, the criterion becomes whether the saving that collects the return gains exceeds the capitalized wage loss. If the pre-robot economy is dynamically efficient, the robot economy inherits its efficiency: the competitive equilibrium with robots is Pareto optimal, and automation policy redistributes welfare across generations rather than correcting a market failure. Because automation compresses the wages out of which households save, better robot technology can reduce robot adoption. Robot taxes redistribute automation's gains; restrictions on automated tasks can destabilize the economy and prevent welfare-enhancing automation.

detail.abstract: We prove that projected inventory level (PIL) policies are asymptotically optimal in a periodic-review lostsales inventory system, with an optimality gap that decays exponentially fast as the replenishment lead time increases. The lost-sales system is a central model in stochastic inventory theory, and understanding the performance and behavior of its simple policies has been a major theme of inventory asymptotic analysis in recent years. PIL policies are based on a simple inventory projection rule and have very strong numerical performance, but their long-lead-time asymptotic optimality under general demand distributions has remained unresolved. We resolve this question for general independent and identically distributed demand with a finite second moment. Our analysis establishes a one-to-one correspondence between finite PIL targets and stable constant-order policies. For each matched pair, actual PIL orders approach the constant order exponentially fast in long-run average expected squared deviation, and the absolute difference between their long-run costs also decays exponentially. Combining the cost comparison with the known exponential asymptotic optimality of constant ordering establishes the exponential asymptotic optimality for PIL policies.

detail.abstract:
It is no longer hypothetical: U.S. government agencies are using AI to write regulations. We therefore must grapple with the intersection of the Administrative Procedure Act (APA) and the undetectability of AI-generated material. To challenge an agency rule for improper agency use of AI under an APA theory, a litigant would need to know which regulations were drafted using AI. But agencies do not acknowledge their use of AI in specific rulemakings and AI-generated text can pass undetected, leaving would-be litigants with an information gap. There are ways in which AI and other outside helpers can legitimately aid the rulemaking process, but policy decisions are human terrain. The APA and current doctrine may not be equipped to hold the line if AI-written preambles can hide in plain sight.

As it stands, the public does not know who writes what in a regulation; we don’t usually know, for example, which staff members worked on any given rule, or whether regulatory language was supplied by outside interests. This opacity—reinforced by the presumption of regularity—might have been acceptable when we could reasonably assume that agencies were in control of writing their rules. Agency use of contractors to write rules has been chipping away at this assumption, but AI undermines it completely. We don’t know who is writing rules anymore because of the availability of algorithmic tools, wide-eyed institutional enthusiasm for AI, and ongoing political hostility towards proceduralism, the civil service, and other good government bulwarks.

title: Community First Responder Activation Reduces the Negative Impact of AED Distance on Bystander Defibrillation After Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest

detail.title: Community First Responder Activation Reduces the Negative Impact of AED Distance on Bystander Defibrillation After Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
detail.abstract: IntroductionEarly defibrillation is critical for survival after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), yet bystander defibrillation remains uncommon despite the availability of automated external defibrillators (AEDs). We investigated whether HeartRunner community first responder activation increased the likelihood of bystander defibrillation and 30-day survival in relation to the distance to the nearest accessible AED.MethodsLinking data from the Danish Cardiac Arrest Registry, Danish AED Network, and HeartRunner application, we identified patients with OHCA eligible for HeartRunner activation during 2017–2021. Using street-network distances to the nearest accessible AED, we examined associations between HeartRunner activation, bystander defibrillation, and 30-day survival using multivariable logistic regression with interaction terms and targeted maximum likelihood estimation (TMLE).ResultsAmong 5,753 OHCAs (median age, 74 years; 64% male; 78% in private locations), HeartRunner activation (41%) was associated with higher bystander defibrillation across AED distances (p-interaction = 0.004), with no interaction for 30-day survival (p-interaction = 0.054). Predicted bystander defibrillation with versus without HeartRunner activation was 9.6% vs 5.5% at Q1 (389 m), 10.0% vs 4.3% at median (717 m), and 13.0% vs 4.8% at Q3 (1,183 m). TMLE estimated a 6.1-percentage-point higher probability of bystander defibrillation (95% CI, 4.5–7.8; p<0.001) and a modest 1.8-percentage-point increase in 30-day survival (95% CI, 0.1–3.6; p=0.038) with HeartRunner activation.ConclusionHeartRunner activation attenuated the decline in bystander defibrillation with increasing AED distance following OHCA, without a corresponding distance interaction for 30-day survival. Overall, TMLE supported higher bystander defibrillation and suggested a modest increase in 30-day survival with HeartRunner activation.

title: Henok's Viability Matrix (HVM): The Viability Window Effect in Loss-Making Growth Firms: Empirical Evidence from SEC Filings

detail.title: Henok's Viability Matrix (HVM): The Viability Window Effect in Loss-Making Growth Firms: Empirical Evidence from SEC Filings

detail.abstract: Loss-making growth firms present a puzzle. Some burn cash for years and still become dominant players. Others burn cash for years and disappear. The difference is not simply the size of the losses. It is the timing of economic improvement relative to the exhaustion of financing capacity. This paper develops a theoretical survival framework centered on what we call the Viability Window Effect. A firm must reach economic viability before its financing runs out. When good economics arrive too late, even attractive business models fail. We operationalize the framework with two accounting proxies. Operating Economic Alpha (αᵤ) is gross margin, used as a proxy for underlying operating economics. Cumulative Equity Absorption Ratio (CEᵣ) is the ratio of negative retained earnings to paid-in capital, interpreted as a proxy for accumulated accounting deficit and cumulative financial burden. The core empirical prediction is that the survival benefit of improving operating economics declines as cumulative financial burden increases. In log-odds terms, the interaction coefficient β₄ is predicted to be negative. We assemble a sample of 67 U.S. technology and biotech firms drawn from SEC filings. The primary interaction model is estimated on 50 firms with complete data for all required variables. The interaction term is negative and statistically significant (β₄ = −44.52, p = 0.004). The full model achieves a pseudo-R² of 0.502 and an AUC of 0.913. A descriptive quadrant analysis reveals that all 20 firms classified as “Strategic Explorers”—high gross margin and high cumulative financial burden—failed. That is a 100% failure rate, with a Wilson 95% confidence interval of 83% to 100%. This is Phase I of a larger research program. We do not claim that 50 firms prove the Viability Window Theory. We find evidence that the predicted interaction appears in real SEC data and that the pattern warrants a more rigorous Phase II test on 300–500 firms with direct time-to-exhaustion measurement.

title: From Spectral-Phase Flow to a Symformic Theory of Control

detail.title: From Spectral-Phase Flow to a Symformic Theory of Control

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests that could have influenced the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required because this study involved no human participants, patients, animals, personal data, or clinical case studies. The empirical component consisted solely of computational simulations using an artificial actant.

detail.abstract: Cybernetics is usually introduced through regulation: a system senses deviation, compares it with some viable condition, and acts. Primary Field Cybernetics (PFC) begins one step earlier. It asks what must remain organized for a system to retain access to the responses by which regulation is possible at all. The theory is derived from two layers of the Symformism research programme. Symformism supplies the ontology: an enduring form is not a frozen object but an organization that preserves identity through change. Dynamical Informational Field Theory (DIFT) supplies a concrete physical architecture: a complex spectral-phase Primary Organizational Field Φ(x, ω, t) supports organized phase flow, constitutive memory, directional accessibility, mobility, impedance, and dynamostatic persistence. In that setting, a mature form is maintained not by the absence of motion but by the continued organization of motion. PFC abstracts this architecture into a general cybernetic proposition. If prior flow can alter memory and the ease with which later trajectories are entered, then a system does not merely choose among a fixed set of responses; through its history it partly reorganizes the practical accessibility of those responses. The domain-neutral variable T acc denotes that history-sensitive access geometry. State control changes what the system is doing now. Access control changes what it will be able to do next. Reflexive control uses a model of the system's own organization to modify that access. Relational metacontrol concerns the still more demanding case in which one actant changes the practical future possibilities of another. This article therefore treats DIFT not as an optional appendix to an otherwise independent cybernetic proposal, but as the physical research branch from which the cybernetic architecture was abstracted. At the same time, the levels are kept epistemically distinct: the field equations are not validated by the later artificial-actant example, and the domain-neutral cybernetic claims do not require that every biological, cognitive, artificial, or institutional system literally instantiate a spectral-phase field. A small numerical illustration isolates one consequence only: prior history can change later reacquisition even under an otherwise matched challenge. Ablation removes that advantage. A further equivalence audit shows that the particular effect does not require a novel two-timescale memory mechanism; a calibrated single trace can reproduce it. The numerical model is therefore an illustration of one accessibility intuition, not a validation of PFC as a whole. The central proposition of Primary Field Cybernetics is that enduring control depends not only on selecting actions, but on preserving and reorganizing the conditions under which viable future action remains accessible.

detail.abstract:
Public procurement rigorously audits bidder licenses, insurance, bonds, and MWBE status, yet routinely incorporates decisive technical specifications without independent evidentiary verification. This institutional blind spot permits privately authored tests, affiliated validators, and unverified life-safety assertions to become binding public purchasing mandates. Once embedded in public solicitations, these proprietary requirements reverse the burden of proof, privatizing the cost of discovering technical truth onto excluded contractors while socializing the cost of failure across taxpayers and building occupants. Consequently, valid technical objections are suppressed unless an unprotected participant risks commercial ruin as a whistleblower.

Drawing on federal antitrust doctrine governing captured standards (ASME v. Hydrolevel; Allied Tube & Conduit), federal acquisition regulations (FAR), and state procurement statutes, this paper demonstrates that whistleblower dependence represents a fundamental governance failure. In response, it proposes an administrative Public Specification Integrity Review—a pre-award truth gate triggered by materially supported technical objections The framework subjects covered requirements to a five-part evidentiary test: provenance, test scope applicability, validator independence, assembly comparability, and objective equivalent-evidence pathways. By replacing post-award litigation and whistleblowing with routine technical due process, this reform prevents the capture of public specifications, restores competitive equity, and ensures taxpayer dollars finance verified performance rather than manufactured authority.

detail.abstract: I study a durable goods monopolist's optimal policy when they cannot commit to future prices in the presence of a competitive resale market where older vintages are traded. I make the substantive assumption that older vintages are imperfect substitutes of the new good, with accelerating drop in substitutability. This gives the monopolist the ability to exercise market power by assortatively sorting customers by their willingness to pay, nudging the highest value buyers to the new good instead of opting for the older vintages. I show the existence and uniqueness of a stationary Markov Perfect Equilibrium under mild regularity conditions, in which the monopolist's charged price lies above the static optimum.

detail.abstract:
Two organizations buy the same AI assistant in the same year, at the same price, for the same number of staff. One spends six weeks before launch writing down which cases the assistant may handle alone, assembling three hundred closed cases with known outcomes, recording who must approve which decisions, and logging the model version in force. The other sends an all-staff email with a training video. Their AI spending is the same number. Their financial statements are indistinguishable. No disclosure either is required to file today will separate them. When the provider replaces the model version, the first can re-run its cases and see what changed; the second finds out when staff start disagreeing with the output, or when a regulator asks how a decision was reached.

This note takes up what a deploying organization should do about that while the reporting rules are unsettled. It is a companion to "The Economics of AI Capital Under Limited Observability" (v9.8, SSRN 7202978) and extends that framework to the reporting question. It reports no new evidence.

Three arguments. First, the failure to record cuts both ways, and neither direction is a claim the underlying framework makes. That framework establishes an observability condition: where a configuration's composition cannot be recovered by inspection, or where its behavior can change with no human act, the record is the only access to what the object currently is. This note draws the reporting consequences. When such an arrangement decays, no required financial disclosure records the loss; when an organization builds capability it can stand behind, none records the gain. A third case is worse than either: a review step performed under load records an approval that the examination behind it did not support. The record is not silent but wrong, and cannot be checked by inspection because every field is properly filled.

Second, the common framing of where this is heading is mistaken in both halves. Recognition is not moving — internally generated AI capability stays off the balance sheet. But IFRS 18, effective for annual periods beginning on or after 1 January 2027, brings management-defined performance measures inside the audited financial statements. An organization publishing an AI-related performance measure will be audited on the management layer while nothing moves onto the balance sheet. The change arrives as a presentation standard rather than a recognition one, which is why it attracts little attention. Eight dated requirements across US and UK regimes are already in force or scheduled.

Third, a small set of actions pays off under every outcome and is cheap now and impossible later. A record of which model version, which prompts, which data, which people and which permissions were in force in a given month can be made that month for the cost of an afternoon. It cannot be made two years later at any price.

The note also introduces recomposition incidence: the location of the economic burden of a change to a productive arrangement, where that change is authored by one party and borne by another. Four features distinguish it from ordinary externality analysis — it is externally timed, unobservable to the bearer, recurring, and contractually normal. A closing section asks what follows if capability keeps compounding toward artificial general intelligence by way of self-improving systems. The capacity to establish what a system does divides into an automated part that gets cheaper as capability improves and a human part bounded by qualified judgment that does not. The scarce factor becomes qualified human judgment, and deployment into consequential decisions is bounded by establishment capacity rather than by capability.

Ten labeled hypotheses are stated with the conditions that would falsify each. Three illustrations are drawn from published state government AI inventories, offered to show that the mechanism is observable in documents anyone can read rather than to establish a pattern from three cases.

title: Neonatal Health and Long-Term Outcomes: Twin-Based Evidence From Linked Scandinavian Registers
affiliations: Stockholm University - Department of Economics, , University College London,  and NHH Norwegian School of Economics - Department of Economics

detail.title: Neonatal Health and Long-Term Outcomes: Twin-Based Evidence From Linked Scandinavian Registers
detail.abstract: This study examines the long-term consequences of neonatal health using three birth anthropometric measures — weight, length, and head circumference — and analyzes their differential associations with outcomes across the life course. Using linked Swedish and Norwegian population registers with follow-up into adulthood, we compare birth measures of singletons and twins and further estimate within-twin-pair fixed-effects models that control for shared genetic and family environmental factors. Our samples comprise up to approximately 679,000 singletons and 10,400 twins in Sweden, and 347,841 singletons and 6,762 twins in Norway, followed into adulthood. We find that different birth measures capture distinct aspects of fetal development with varying predictive validity across outcome domains. Birth length emerges as the strongest predictor of health outcomes (infant mortality, adult height), consistent with its role as a cumulative indicator of skeletal growth throughout gestation. Birth weight retains stronger associations with cognitive and educational outcomes (grade point average [GPA], years of schooling) in conditional models. Head circumference shows weak and inconsistent associations across specifications. Using within-pair head circumference differences to classify twins as symmetrically versus asymmetrically growth restricted, we find that symmetric intrauterine growth restriction is associated with substantially worse long-term outcomes than asymmetric restriction. In Norwegian twin pairs, growth restriction is associated with lower general cognitive ability (measured at military enlistment) relative to the unaffected co-twin; this within-pair deficit is more than twice as large for symmetric as for asymmetric restriction. We also document significant intergenerational transmission of birth anthropometrics, suggesting both environmental and genetic contributions. Finally, our register-based design with near-complete population coverage minimizes selection bias and attrition while providing statistical power for within-pair analyses across multiple outcomes. Exclusive reliance on birth weight may obscure important information about early-gestation developmental insults.

title: The Role of AI in Online Reviews
affiliations: The Hebrew University of Jerusalem - Business School, Hebrew University of Jerusalem and Hebrew University of Jerusalem - Center for the Study of Rationality

detail.title: The Role of AI in Online Reviews
detail.abstract: The rapid adoption of large language models (LLMs) creates new opportunities for strategic content generation on online platforms, including potentially harmful forms of manipulation that may undermine platform effectiveness and reshape platform dynamics. However, measuring such activity is difficult because AI-generated content is rarely directly observable. We introduce an empirical approach that leverages discrete LLM supply shocks - abrupt changes in model prices and capabilities, and contrasts verified with non-verified reviews to identify changes in platform activity associated with generative AI supply improvements. We apply this approach to more than 13 million reviews from Trustpilot, one of the leading online platforms for business reviews. A robust finding is that following LLM supply shocks, unverified reviews shift toward greater negativity: more 1-stars, fewer 5-stars, and lower ratings, with effects driven primarily by new model releases and concentrated among firms with the lowest and highest review volumes, suggesting that strategic AI use may reshape platform competition dynamics. We further find that LLM supply shocks trigger short, concentrated bursts of review activity. Together, these findings suggest that generative AI is already reshaping how reputation and competition operate on online platforms.
